Burkina : 82 nouvelles compétences pour renforcer les services postaux
items.description: La 51e promotion des stagiaires de l'Ecole nationale des postes a achevé sa formation. Ce 4 novembre 2026, les 82 stagiaires ont reçu leurs parchemins de fin de formation au cours d'une cérémonie de sortie de promotion organisée pour l'occasion. La cérémonie de sortie de promotion a été parrainée par la ministre de la transition digitale, des postes et des communications électroniques, Aminata Zerbo/Sabané, représentée par son secrétaire général. La 51e promotion de l'École nationale des postes compte 18 contrôleurs des services postaux et financiers, 54 agents de bureau et 10 agents d'exploitation. Après une année de formation théorique et pratique, ponctuée de stages d'immersion dans les structures opérationnelles de la Poste Burkina Faso, les récipiendaires sont désormais prêts à intégrer le monde professionnel. L'École nationale des postes a célébré, ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la sortie de sa 51e promotion. Ils sont appelés à contribuer au renforcement et à la modernisation des services postaux et financiers au Burkina Faso. Selon la directrice de l'Ecole nationale des postes, Koumbo Rahja Barry, cette promotion affiche un taux de réussite global de 100 %. Elle a également souligné les performances des majors, qui ont obtenu respectivement 18,35/20 chez les contrôleurs, 18,26/20 chez les agents d'exploitation et 18,93/20 chez les agents de bureau. Koumbo Rahja Barry, directrice générale de l'Ecole nationale des postes a indiqué qu'un taux de réussite de 100% a été enregistré pour la 51e promotion La formation des nouveaux diplômés a essentiellement porté sur la maîtrise des opérations postales et financières, la relation client, l'utilisation des outils numériques, ainsi que les exigences d'éthique, de déontologie et de qualité de service. L'objectif étant selon la directrice de mettre à la disposition de la poste des professionnels capables de s'adapter aux mutations du secteur et d'accompagner sa transformation. Les majors des trois sections ont reçu leurs parchemins des mains du Dr Michel Jonas Somé Elle a invité les stagiaires à mettre en pratique au quotidien les compétences acquises, pour le bonheur des clients. « Je vous invite à respecter les procédures, à cultiver l'esprit d'équipe, à faire preuve de discrétion dans le traitement des informations, à demeurer attentifs aux besoins des clients. Gardez toujours à l'esprit que derrière chaque courrier, chaque colis et chaque opération se trouve un client qui attend un service fiable, rapide, accessible et sécurisé », a-t-elle lancé. Venu présider la cérémonie au nom de la ministre de la transition digitale, des postes et des communications électroniques, Aminata Zerbo/Sabané, le secrétaire général du ministère, Dr Michel Jonas Somé, a rappelé les défis auxquels fait face le secteur postal. Il a notamment évoqué la transformation numérique, l'évolution des habitudes des usagers, l'essor du commerce électronique et des services financiers numériques, ainsi que les exigences croissantes en matière de rapidité et de qualité. Dr Michel Jonas Somé, représentant de la ministre des postes a invité les lauréats à cultiver l'intégrité Il a également insisté sur le rôle que la poste est appelée à jouer dans le rapprochement des services publics des populations, notamment à travers les maisons de citoyens, qui visent à faciliter l'accès aux services postaux et financiers ainsi qu'aux services administratifs dématérialisés. À l'endroit des nouveaux diplômés, le représentant de la ministre a formulé cinq principales recommandations : cultiver l'intégrité et le sens du devoir, placer la satisfaction de l'usager au cœur des priorités, faire preuve de curiosité et d'ouverture à l'innovation, privilégier la rigueur et le professionnalisme et enfin développer l'esprit d'équipe et la solidarité professionnelle. Au nom des récipiendaires, la déléguée générale des stagiaires, Nelly Yasmina Bambara/Sawadogo a pris l'engagement de mettre les compétences acquises au service de la Poste Burkina Faso. Elle a notamment souligné que la qualité du service postal ne repose pas uniquement sur la maîtrise des procédures et des outils techniques, mais exige également l'écoute des clients, la courtoisie, le respect des délais et la confidentialité. Les récipiendaires par la voix de leur déléguée, Nelly Yasmina Sawadogo se sont engagés à être des volontaires photo la défense de la poste Les nouveaux diplômés se sont également engagés à être de véritables « volontaires pour la défense de la Poste Burkina Faso », mais également des acteurs de sa transformation et de sa modernisation. « Nous réaffirmons notre entière disponibilité ainsi que notre ferme détermination à mettre les compétences acquises, notre engagement et notre motivation au service du secteur postal. Fort de la formation reçue et pleinement conscients des enjeux qui se dessinent, nous nous tenons prêts à relever avec responsabilité et détermination les défis présents et futurs auxquels notre service sera confronté », a affirmé Nelly Yasmina Sawadogo. Il faut noter que la 51e promotion des stagiaires de l'Ecole nationale des postes a été parrainée par Dr Pasteur Poda, président du Conseil de régulation de l'ARCEP. la 51e promotion des stagiaires de l'Ecole nationale des postes a été parrainée par Dr Pasteur Poda, président du Conseil de régulation de l'ARCEP Armelle Ouédraogo Lefaso.net Crédit photo : Bonaventure Paré

items.title: Sécurité routière : à Kindia, Ousmane Gaoual Diallo tire la sonnette d’alarme face aux accidents
items.description: La recrudescence des accidents de la circulation continue de susciter de vives préoccupations au sein des autorités guinéennes. En tournée dans la région de Kindia, le ministre des Transports, Ousmane Gaoual Diallo, a rencontré les autorités administratives et sécuritaires, les organisations syndicales ainsi que les professionnels du transport routier. Cette concertation, tenue au siège du gouvernorat, visait à renforcer la mobilisation des différents acteurs autour des impératifs de sécurité routière. À cette occasion, le ministre a justifié cette démarche par la nécessité d'impliquer davantage les parties prenantes dans la prévention des accidents « Notre tournée dans la région de Kindia vise à rencontrer les différentes autorités administratives et sécuritaires, les syndicats, les associations et tous les acteurs de la sécurité routière, afin d’échanger avec eux sur les préoccupations du gouvernement quant à la recrudescence des accidents de la circulation », a expliqué Ousmane Gaoual Diallo. Le ministre a notamment fait état d’un bilan humain préoccupant, évoquant 251 victimes alors que l’année 2026 n’est pas encore arrivée à son terme. Il a, dans la même dynamique, appelé les différents partenaires à redoubler d’efforts, particulièrement à l’approche des festivités de fin d’année. L’immatriculation et l’assurance des véhicules figurent également parmi les exigences rappelées aux professionnels du transport « Nous avons rappelé l’exigence d’immatriculer et d’assurer les véhicules qui prennent la route, parce que tout cela contribue à l’amélioration de la sécurité des citoyens. Le gouvernement est attentif aux différentes préoccupations qui nous sont remontées et, dans la mesure du possible, nous allons apporter des réponses », a-t-il assuré. Au niveau régional, cette rencontre nourrit également des ambitions en matière de prévention. Komoro Mohamed, chef du bureau régional des transports terrestres de Kindia, affiche un objectif particulièrement ambitieux pour les prochaines années « C’est de faire de Kindia une zone zéro accident d’ici 2027. C’est ce que nous souhaitons. Mon sentiment est très bon après le passage de Monsieur le ministre. Le message est qu’il faut être prudent sur la route », a-t-il déclaré. À travers cette rencontre, les autorités entendent renforcer la responsabilisation des usagers et promouvoir une culture de prudence sur les routes, avec pour finalité, la réduction des accidents et la préservation des vies humaines.

items.title: Govt says Islamabad's One Constitution Avenue to be turned into a five-star hotel
items.description: The federal government on Wednesday said that a joint investigation team had revealed that Islamabad’s One Constitution Avenue was built on “irregularities and rigging” and announced that the residential building will soon be turned into a five-star hotel. The building, a skyscraper in the federal capital that houses residential apartments, had its lease cancelled by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) due to the company behind the project defaulting on payments. The decision was upheld by the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in April. The building was initially supposed to be a five-star hotel project; however, instead of functioning as a five-star hotel, it was converted into residential apartments and commercial areas. The IHC’s order led to the mass evictions of residents in May, following which Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif formed a joint investigation team (JIT) to probe the matter. Addressing a press conference on Wednesday alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the JIT presented its report to the federal cabinet today, noting that the project was fraudulent. He said that the report had input from the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), the Federal Investigation Agency, the Federal Board of Revenue, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, the Intelligence Bureau and Inter-Services Intelligence. “They carefully assessed this project and presented the report, and it was approved,” Iqbal said. “The JIT has clearly identified that the project was created based on irregularity and rigging and that the bidding process was manipulated.” Iqbal added that, according to the report, rules were ignored to provide benefits and the company which was given the lease had no rightful claim. “In this whole matter, the CDA was found complicit, and similarly, the conditions of the bank guarantee were removed to provide benefits to the developers,” he stated. “The work which was carried out was conducted in a very suspicious manner and the apartments were sold illegally.” He noted that the project was initially approved as a five-star hotel two decades ago, but later it was turned into apartments. “The JIT has identified Abdul Hafeez Sheikh, who has been called the mastermind and was found to be in connivance with CDA officials,” the planning minister added. “CDA officers such as Kamran Lashari, who was chairman at the time, Dr Faisal Awan, Azhar Ali Chaudhry, Brigadier (retired) Nasrullah and Marhoom Rai Nawaz Kharal were found to be colluding in fraud,” he said. Iqbal said that as a result of the scheme, the national exchequer suffered losses, while the aforementioned people “gained financially and defrauded the Pakistani people of their invested capital”. “The JIT recommended that Sheikh and his company be blacklisted from future public projects and that proceedings be launched against him,” the minister added. It was further recommended that the project be reviewed and work undertaken to achieve its original purpose as a hotel. Additionally, the report recommended that the project be started anew and auctioned in a transparent manner, he said. “Security clearance and clearance from other institutions should also be sought so that future projects have a steady framework to prevent this type of fraud from happening again,” Iqbal said, adding that fire safety and other protocols must also be ensured. He added that according to the JIT, the project should be renamed, as the name ‘One Constitution Avenue’ was the same address as the finance ministry. “They used this address for marketing purposes only,” the minister asserted. “There will be action taken against those found involved in fraud. The government has a responsibility to protect those who were robbed or swindled.” Iqbal said it was decided that those defrauded would receive compensation, their principal investments would be refunded and payments would be adjusted against their Kibor interest “so they do not suffer losses”. “It was also recommended that the CDA and its ordinance be overhauled and that an independent master plan commission be formed to shut the door on such fraud in the future,” he announced. Iqbal added that all of the records must be digitised and officers should be rotated between the state planning, enforcement and building control departments every two years. “People have held offices for 20 years and opened offices of fraud. With this constant rotation, it will close the door on these corrupt projects,” he explained. “In the same way, pre-audit auctions and contracts from third parties will be consulted, and in light of this JIT report, NAB has been ordered to take action against anyone involved in this project, and those who facilitated it,” Iqbal said. Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also addressed a press conference on Wednesday and said that the government had now regained possession of the skyscraper, vowing to turn the building into a five-star hotel within months. “In official documents, we always had possession of this building, and after the cabinet’s approval, it is now legally in our possession,” Naqvi maintained. He regretted that the government’s decision to regain control of the building earlier this year had been portrayed as a “crime”, decrying how Islamabad’s land had been infringed upon. “We will try our best to convert this building into a five-star hotel in months,” the interior minister announced, reaffirming that this had been the project’s primary objective. “There is a severe shortage of hotels in Islamabad. We will soon try to make an agreement with a large chain of hotels and convert this building into a five-star hotel,” he stated. He commended the CDA chairman and legal team for pursuing this case; however, Naqvi also reproached the CDA for being at fault. “NAB will tell who is responsible,” he said. “As per JIT recommendations, we will try to make rightful payments to the occupants,” Naqvi said. “This is binding for us after the report.” The interior minister said he was grateful to PM Shehbaz, recalling that the prime minister had assured him that the right decision would be taken. Naqvi further said that a residents’ committee, which was overseeing the building’s affairs, had been abolished. “A CDA member will look after the building’s matters from now on,” he said, reiterating that the hotel would be operational soon and be a “gift to the people of Islamabad”.

items.title: Majority, Minority Chief Whips demand end to insurance exemption for government vehicles
items.description: The Majority and Minority Chief Whips have demanded an end to the insurance exemption for government vehicles, warning that it leaves road crash victims facing difficult compensation claims. In a joint statement delivered in Parliament on November 4, Majority Chief Whip Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor and Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh urged government to amend the law. They also called for immediate insurance cover for state fleets. “We demand of the trader, the taxi driver and the tricycle rider what the State does not demand of itself.” The Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Act, 1958 (Act 42) requires motorists to have third-party insurance. However, it exempts vehicles owned by, or exclusively employed in the service of, government when used for government purposes. The two whips argued that this exemption undermines equal treatment and public trust. “A child is no less an orphan because the vehicle was owned by the state.” They cited findings referenced in Parliament in 2022 indicating that between 98 and 99 per cent of more than 18,000 government vehicles were uninsured. They also pointed to a July 2024 crash involving an uninsured GETFund school bus near Koforidua. According to the statement, the victims received no insurance benefit. The whips challenged the argument that the government could pay compensation directly instead of buying insurance. “However, self-insurance without a ring-fenced fund is a promise on paper.” They said victims could be forced to petition a ministry, sue the Attorney-General and wait for funding that might not be available. Insurance, they argued, would give victims enforceable rights while making government’s costs more predictable. Their demands include amendments to Act 42, developed with the National Insurance Commission and the Attorney-General, to remove the exemption. They also want all ministries, departments and agencies to insure their fleets immediately and register them on the Motor Insurance Database. The statement further called for insurance premiums to be included in the 2027 Budget and for a published audit of government vehicles and their insurance status. The whips acknowledged that successive administrations had left the exemption untouched. They urged a collective response. “Mr Speaker, a State that asks its citizens to insure must be willing to insure itself.”

items.title: ₦70,000 Transport Allowance: Labour veterans wade into crisis between NLC, TUC
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — Labour veterans from the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have intervened in the face-off between the President of the NLC, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and the TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo. The two labour leaders have recently traded words over the recent approval of ₦70,000 by the Federal Government to cushion the effect of high transportation costs occasioned by the removal of fuel subsidy. The rift between the two leaders degenerated into personal attacks on national television, a situation that has affected unity within the labour sector. Worried by the development, labour veterans met to bring the situation under control. Speaking on Wednesday in Abuja at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), Comrade Wabba said the labour veterans had been able to arrest any form of hostility between the two leaders. The former NLC President told journalists that veterans from the two labour centres had met to resolve what he described as a family misunderstanding between the two centres. He said the veterans emphasised that workers’ organisations must remain united because they share a single objective and aim. The former President of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC) said all hostilities had been ordered to stop, explaining that the goal is to prevent future occurrences through formal dialogue. He said: “It’s a family misunderstanding between the two centres, and we have made it clear that workers’ organisations are supposed to be one because the objective is one and the aim is one. “So, that seeming misunderstanding has escalated, and we have said all hostilities should stop. We will actually try to meet with them to see what happened and how future occurrences can also be prevented. “So, basically, I can tell you for sure that veterans from both sides—TUC and NLC—namely Peter Esele, Bobboi Kaigama, Hassan Sunmonu, Abdulwaheed Omar, and my humble self, actually met and tried to look at the issue. We said we would meet formally when all of them are available because we just communicated among ourselves, the veterans, and we communicated with them, and they mutually accepted. “The TUC General Secretary was here; I was here; the NLC President was here. All of us embraced ourselves and said, ‘Well, it’s a family issue.’ Therefore, we have also said members of the press should not actually try to advance issues that are not there because, even in your immediate family, you can have some internal issues. “But that internal issue is certainly meant to be resolved, and we are working towards that very effectively because that is the hallmark of trade unionism: to resolve issues, even with our employers, through dialogue and social dialogue. So, basically, it is an issue we have practised, and therefore we will try to now put it into action.” The former NLC President said some of the protagonists in the matter had travelled, adding that once they returned, “we will be able to have that platform to address the issue.” “But for the meantime, we said we don’t see the necessity of further talking to the press because that, in itself, does not bring any solution.” Speaking earlier, the NLC President, Comrade Ajaero, said the agreed ₦70,000 transport intervention had become secured for workers and that, when discussions for a new minimum wage begin, the money would form part of what would be added. items.title: Abu Jinapor and Minority shall not be silenced; Ablakwa was loud when in opposition – Afenyo-Markin
items.description: The Minority has declared that the Member of Parliament for Damongo, Samuel Abu Jinapor, will not be silenced following his removal from the parliamentary chamber, insisting that Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa must also be prepared to face scrutiny. The Minority Leader, Alexander Afenyo-Markin, said the caucus would not relent in holding the government and its appointees accountable, drawing comparisons with Mr Ablakwa’s conduct while in opposition. Addressing the media on Wednesday, November 4, Mr Afenyo-Markin argued that the Foreign Affairs Minister was vocal and uncompromising in demanding accountability from the previous government and should not be shielded from similar scrutiny now that he was in office. “Honourable Jinapor shall not be silenced. The caucus shall not be silenced. We shall hold the government and its functionaries accountable as Ghanaians have entrusted us to do,” he said. He added: “Honourable Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa himself was never silenced. In opposition, he was loud. He never compromised. Therefore, this is not a time to shield him.” His comments followed Tuesday’s removal of the Member of Parliament for Damongo, Samuel Abu Jinapor, from the Chamber by a Parliamentary Marshal after he refused to withdraw an allegation against Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. Read also: Abu Jinapor escorted out of Parliament after refusing to withdraw passport allegation against Ablakwa Mr Afenyo-Markin challenged the Foreign Affairs Minister to publicly defend the principles he championed while in opposition, insisting that his current position should not exempt him from accountability. He said the Minority would remain committed to its oversight responsibilities regardless of the pressure it faced. “Whatever pressure comes our way, we shall return to our duty with steady hearts, with clear voices, with unbroken resolve. This is the mighty minority,” he said. Describing the caucus as small in numbers but firm in conviction, the Minority Leader reaffirmed its determination to continue speaking on behalf of Ghanaians. “This is the mighty minority. We are few but firm in conviction. This is who we are.”

items.title: KNUST, Norwegian consulting firm explore partnership on student exchange, research
items.description: The Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) has initiated discussions with the Norwegian African Relations Consult (NARC) to establish a strategic partnership aimed at promoting international academic exchange and collaborative research between Ghana and Norway. The development follows a consultative meeting on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, between KNUST Vice-Chancellor, Professor Christian Agyare, and a delegation from NARC led by its Chief Executive Officer, Joseph Kyei-Boateng. Speaking at the meeting, Mr Kyei-Boateng, a KNUST alumnus and former media practitioner, said NARC was established to bridge academic and development gaps between countries in the Global South and developed nations in the Global North. “Norway and Ghana are bigger, so we have to start somewhere, and this is why we are narrowing the partnership through KNUST and potential universities in Norway,” he said. “As the adage goes, charity begins at home; as an alumnus, it is like coming back to my former university to initiate this cooperation,” he added. He said the proposed partnership would focus on student and staff exchanges, joint scientific research and capacity-building initiatives aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly in quality education, health, innovation and sustainable technology. Mr Kyei-Boateng, formerly of the Graphic Communications Group, said funding for the initiative was expected to come from the Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation (NORAD), under Norway’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, following the submission of joint proposals. The Vice-Chancellor, Professor Christian Agyare, welcomed the initiative, saying it aligned with KNUST’s strategic plan, Plan 2K35, which focuses on mutually beneficial partnerships and seeks to move the university “from excellence to eminence” through global impact. “We are happy to have this arranged. Our key interest is in student and staff exchanges, as well as joint research collaborations,” he said. He added that the proposed framework’s inclusion of all categories of staff would provide opportunities for exposure and motivation across the university to advance its strategic vision. Highlighting areas where Ghana could benefit from Norway’s experience, Professor Agyare identified natural resource management, sustainable oil production and technology transfer as potential areas for collaboration. He, however, requested that NARC submit a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for review by KNUST’s Legal Office and International Programmes Office (IPO) to formally initiate the proposed partnership. According to him, the MoU would establish clear targets, timelines and responsibilities, paving the way for joint project proposals and student internship placements. He commended Mr Kyei-Boateng for seeking to give back to his alma mater.

items.title: NNPC posts N3.49trn profit in nine months
items.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja ABUJA — The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) recorded a cumulative Profit After Tax (PAT) of N3.494 trillion between January and September 2026, following an 18.1 per cent increase in its September profit to N509 billion. The September profit rose from N431 billion recorded in August, according to the company’s September 2026 Monthly Operations and Financial Report. The latest figures bring NNPC’s cumulative profit for the first nine months of 2026 to N3.494 trillion. A breakdown of the performance showed that the company recorded profits of N385 billion in January, N136 billion in February, N276 billion in March, N481 billion in April, N462 billion in May, N535 billion in June, N279 billion in July, N431 billion in August and N509 billion in September. The report also showed that NNPC generated N33.152 trillion in revenue during the nine-month period. Its September revenue stood at N4.608 trillion, representing a 23.3 per cent increase from the N3.737 trillion recorded in August. Monthly revenue figures showed that the company generated N2.571 trillion in January, N2.680 trillion in February, N2.774 trillion in March, N4.971 trillion in April, N4.335 trillion in May, N4.389 trillion in June and N3.087 trillion in July. On its statutory obligations, NNPC disclosed that payments to the Federation Account and other statutory remittances rose to N11.14 trillion between January and September. The amount represents an increase of 17.4 per cent, or N1.65 trillion, over the N9.49 trillion recorded between January and August. On the operational front, average crude oil and condensate production stood at 1.70 million barrels per day in September. Natural gas production also increased to 7,789 million standard cubic feet per day, compared with 7,680 million standard cubic feet per day recorded in August. Total hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil, condensate and natural gas equivalent, averaged 3.04 million barrels of oil equivalent per day during the period. The company further reported 100 per cent availability of its upstream pipeline infrastructure in September. On gas infrastructure projects, NNPC said the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) Gas Pipeline had achieved 100 per cent completion, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline was 95 per cent complete. It added that the OB3 River Niger Crossing pipeline had been commissioned and operationalised. According to the company, collaboration with relevant stakeholders was ongoing to accelerate construction and pre-commissioning activities on the AKK project, with a target of delivering early gas supply to Abuja before the end of 2026. items.title: NAIMOS only embarks on lawful arrests, but it may go offensive where necessary – Paa Kwesi Schandorf
items.description: The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has said the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) does not embark on operations with aggression but may take decisive action to protect its officers when faced with imminent threats. The Ministry’s Media Relations Officer, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, said the task force’s primary responsibility was to enforce the law through the arrest of persons involved in illegal mining activities. Speaking in an interview with JoyNews , Mr Schandorf explained that NAIMOS was expected to operate within the confines of the law and avoid actions that could be considered excessive. He said, however, said that the task force would not hesitate to take appropriate action if its officers faced threats that could result in death or injury during operations. “When it comes to community obstructions or resistance, NAIMOS’ first and principal point of call or consideration is to ensure that it acts within the remits of the law and doesn’t do anything that can be construed as an excessive reaction,” he said. He added that the circumstances surrounding each operation would determine the level of response required from the officers. “That notwithstanding, when the task force at any material moment is faced with imminent threats, threats that could actually lead to the loss of life of members of the task force or injury, appropriate and proportionate action will be taken,” he stated. Mr Schandorf said it was therefore wrong to suggest that NAIMOS entered communities with an aggressive approach as its starting point. According to him, the task force’s mandate is primarily to arrest illegal miners and ensure that the law is enforced. “So, it is not a case that NAIMOS goes into any community with aggression in the very first place. No, their task and their mandate is basically to enforce by way of arresting illegal miners,” he explained. The Ministry’s spokesperson further explained that although the task force was expected to carry out its operations peacefully, it could resort to other decisive measures if the safety of its officers was threatened. He said such action would be guided by necessity and proportionality rather than aggression. “But if at any point in the lawful execution of that mandate or duty, it emerges that NAIMOS has to employ other decisive actions to save the lives of its members, I think it will be done appropriately,” he said. Mr Schandorf also referred to comments by the sector minister, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, who has indicated that members of the task force are entitled to defend themselves when circumstances make it necessary. “In any case, the sector minister, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, has stated clearly that the NAIMOS task force is at liberty to defend themselves where it is extremely necessary,” he added. He said that the task force would not resort to force without justification, insisting that the nature of the threat would determine the appropriate response. “And so, it will be based on necessity. If there is no need for any intense action, NAIMOS typically will just do its civil operations and then arrest those who have to be arrested,” Mr Schandorf said.

items.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital. The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed. The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting. According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy. The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained. Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled. The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area. In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident. Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.” The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state. It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.” It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels. Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.” The post Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: AFCON 2027Q: Ghana to host Somalia in Sekondi
items.description: The Sekondi Sports Stadium will host Ghana’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifier against Somalia, the Ghana Football Association has confirmed. This follows a temporary approval by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) for the match slated for November 12, 2026. GFA President Kurt Okraku disclosed this on Wednesday afternoon, when he met Parliament’s Select Committee on Youth, Sports and Culture. CAF could only grant temporary approval for the facility since significant aspects of the stadium are yet to meet standard licensing requirements. The recent renovation works only covered the replacement of the roof, the replacement of all seats, the washrooms, the VIP area, and the scoreboard. To comply with CAF standards, the Sekondi Sports Stadium must expand its dressing room to 24 lockers per team, install water heaters, and other fittings required for a modern dressing room. CAF also requires fully functional drainage and irrigation systems that support a quality playing surface. It also requires a functional CCTV surveillance system, automated access control, or electronic spectator counting. The stadium’s mechanisms for crowd management, emergency evacuation systems, media facilities, and security systems would all have to be fixed. At the moment, the media stand only had foldable, plastic seats. To meet CAF standards, the media section would need reliable internet connectivity, with significant enhancements to the conference room for post-match engagements. The media requirements include a permanent photographer’s area and a setup behind the goalposts with proper seats, power extensions, and Wi-Fi/cables. Although these are yet to be fixed, CAF has granted approval for what will be the stadium’s second competitive game since reopening. items.title: NAIMOS to receive GH¢200m in 2027 budget – Paa Kwesi Schandorf
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) is expected to receive GH¢200 million in the 2027 Budget to strengthen its operational capacity and support efforts to combat illegal mining. The Media Relations Officer at the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, said President John Dramani Mahama had assured that the amount would be committed to the secretariat to ensure it was adequately resourced to confront illegal mining activities. Speaking to journalists, he said the government had developed an elaborate plan to provide the secretariat with the resources needed to implement its operational strategy effectively. Mr Schandorf expressed confidence that the proposed allocation would be sufficient to support NAIMOS’ operations, based on the requirements outlined in its operational strategy. “There is a very elaborate plan to ensure that NAIMOS is adequately resourced. President Mahama has assured that GH¢200 million is going to be committed to NAIMOS in the 2027 budget. Based on the operational strategy, it will be more than adequate to ensure that it is well-resourced to confront some of these issues when they come,” he said. The proposed funding is expected to strengthen the secretariat’s ability to respond to illegal mining activities and sustain its operations as the government intensifies efforts to tackle the menace. NAIMOS is a key component of the government’s efforts to combat illegal mining, commonly known as galamsey, through coordinated enforcement operations and interventions.

items.title: Atiku vows to restore fuel subsidy, reopen borders, reduce pilgrimage costs
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to restore petroleum subsidy, tackle insecurity, reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries and reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful if elected president in 2027. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the pledges on Wednesday during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he outlined his proposed measures to address the country’s economic challenges, insecurity and declining standard of living. He said his administration would prioritise the welfare of Nigerians, adding that restoring petroleum subsidy would be among the measures considered to ease the burden of rising fuel prices and reduce transportation costs and the prices of essential commodities. The former vice-president also promised to take decisive steps to address insecurity across the country, protect lives and property and restore confidence in the nation’s security architecture. He said Nigerians deserved to live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities. On the economy, Atiku pledged to reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries to revive economic activities, strengthen regional trade and improve the livelihoods of communities dependent on cross-border commerce. He said the move would create opportunities for traders, farmers and other economic operators while strengthening Nigeria’s commercial relations with neighbouring countries. The ADC candidate also promised to reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful, arguing that the cost of religious journeys should not constitute an overwhelming burden for ordinary Nigerians. He said his proposed administration would introduce policies to improve citizens’ welfare, expand economic opportunities and address the hardship confronting households. Atiku urged Nigerians to support the ADC in the 2027 presidential election, saying the party would provide an alternative direction for the country. Senator David Mark speaks Speaking at the rally, the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, said the reception he witnessed from the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport to Sokoto metropolis indicated widespread support for the party in the state. He expressed confidence that the people of Sokoto would vote for Atiku and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections. Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal speaks Also addressing the gathering, former Sokoto State Governor, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration, accusing it of worsening poverty, hunger and insecurity across the country. Tambuwal said the ruling party had failed to provide the leadership required to address Nigeria’s economic and security challenges. He argued that Nigerians were facing severe economic difficulties, widespread hunger and persistent insecurity, insisting that the situation underscored the need for a change in leadership. The former governor urged Nigerians to embrace the ADC as a political alternative, calling on them to support Atiku in the forthcoming election. In his remarks, the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State assured Atiku of massive electoral support from the state, declaring that the party would mobilise its grassroots structures to secure votes for him in 2027. “Your Excellency, Atiku Abubakar, Sokoto is your home, and we will prove that in 2027,” he said, amid cheers from party supporters. The governorship candidate said the party would work to translate the enthusiasm surrounding Atiku’s candidacy into votes, urging members and supporters to remain united and committed to the ADC’s electoral campaign. He described the campaign flag-off as an important step in the party’s preparations for the 2027 general elections. The post Atiku vows to restore fuel subsidy, reopen borders, reduce pilgrimage costs appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le démocrate qui a conquis le Texas en opposant « l’amour » à Trump
items.description: Dans l’une des courses les plus suivies et les plus coûteuses de l’histoire politique américaine, le candidat démocrate James Talarico a battu hier le procureur général républicain Ken Paxton, proche allié de Donald Trump, avec une avance de plus d’un million de voix . Pour la première fois depuis 1988, un démocrate remporte un siège de sénateur au Texas. Cette victoire historique s’inscrit dans une vague nationale , mais elle présente une singularité : elle constitue, plus qu’ailleurs, une défaite pour Elon Musk, qui avait investi quelque 200 millions de dollars dans cette course . Elle marque aussi le lancement d’une carrière potentiellement présidentielle pour l’une des figures les plus étonnantes de ce cycle politique, à laquelle nous avions consacré dès le mois de mars un grand portrait doctrine . Ancien enseignant et séminariste presbytérien, James Talarico incarne parfaitement la « stratégie de l’hétérodoxie » préconisée par le rapport Deciding to win : prônant une critique populiste des institutions et de l’IA, centriste pragmatique sur les frontières ou les énergies fossiles, il fait de la Bible le cœur d’un nouveau progressisme profondément religieux, qui n’oppose plus la gauche à la droite mais « ceux d’en haut » à « ceux d’en bas ». Ce discours, intégralement charpenté autour d’une série de références bibliques – de David contre Goliath aux marchands chassés du Temple –, a été prononcé derrière un pupitre où la devise « Love thy neighbor » sert de cadre narratif pour proclamer un nouveau style politique, dont il entend désormais faire l’épreuve au Sénat, où il promet, comme le « rabbin aux pieds nus », de « renverser la table ». Nous venons de reprendre le Texas. Nous venons de prouver que tout l’argent du monde ne fait pas le poids face au peuple texan. Nous venons de montrer qu’une politique de la division ne fait pas le poids face à une politique de l’amour. Et nous venons d’envoyer un message à tous les méga-donateurs milliardaires, à tous les méga-donateurs multimilliardaires, à tous les défenseurs corrompus de ce système politique défaillant, dans cet État, dans ce pays : le pouvoir appartient au peuple. Cela me rappelle cette histoire tirée des Écritures, celle d’un jeune berger qui affronte un géant. Pendant quarante jours, Goliath le nargue et le provoque. Le jour du combat, il se présente en armure complète. Il porte tant d’armes qu’il a besoin que quelqu’un d’autre porte son bouclier. Dans cette campagne, nous avons affronté nos propres Goliaths : l’homme le plus riche du monde, l’homme le plus puissant du monde et l’establishment de Washington D.C. tout entier. David… David n’était ni aussi grand ni aussi fort que Goliath, il n’avait pas autant d’armes. Mais il avait l’espoir, il avait la foi. Et il avait une fronde. Ma fronde, c’était vous. Ma fronde, c’était le peuple texan. Et ce soir, nous avons vaincu Goliath. Les Écritures m’ont appris – ma propre vie m’a appris – qu’il faut toujours parier sur l’outsider. Avant d’être un homme politique, j’étais professeur dans une école publique. J’enseignais l’anglais au collège Rhodes, dans le West Side de San Antonio. Et comme je le dis toujours, enseigner au collège est la meilleure façon de se préparer à la politique. Le West Side est un quartier magnifique et historique. C’est aussi l’un des quartiers les plus pauvres de tout l’État du Texas. Chaque jour, mes élèves luttaient héroïquement pour surmonter un système truqué. Mes élèves n’étaient pas seulement des enfants ; c’étaient des survivants, des rêveurs, des battants. Je le voyais dans leurs yeux chaque jour : cette détermination inébranlable, cet esprit indomptable. En grandissant, j’ai vu cette même combativité chez ma mère, une fille de pasteur originaire de Laredo qui avait quitté la maison à 19 ans. Elle s’était installée à Austin et avait rencontré mon père biologique, un jeune homme de 21 ans qui avait abandonné le lycée et dont les problèmes d’alcoolisme menaient parfois à des violences. Une nuit, il s’est à nouveau montré violent. Mais cette nuit-là, cette nuit-là, l’amour de ma mère s’est dressé face à cette violence. Elle a chargé toutes nos affaires dans sa petite Ford Escort. Elle m’a emmené à l’hôtel où elle travaillait. Elle a supplié le gérant de nous laisser rester dans l’une des chambres jusqu’à ce que nous trouvions un petit appartement à East Austin. Il n’y avait pas de place pour une chambre d’enfant. Alors je dormais dans un lit de bébé installé dans son placard. Et elle était tellement fière de ce placard. Elle l’avait décoré avec des photos et des jouets. Personne n’allait lui dire que ce n’était pas une chambre de bébé. Toujours. Pariez toujours sur l’outsider. Nous étions les outsiders dans cette course. Nous avons affronté près de quarante ans de doutes et de désillusions. Nous avons fait face à plus de 300 millions de dollars dépensés contre nous, un montant supérieur à celui de n’importe quelle campagne sénatoriale de l’histoire américaine. Nous avons affronté toutes les publicités négatives, campagnes de dénigrement, bots étrangers et autres deepfakes générés par l’IA que l’argent peut acheter. Ces attaques étaient les derniers hurlements d’un establishment agonisant. Le râle d’un statu quo qui sait que ses jours sont comptés. Ils ont joué sale parce qu’ils étaient désespérés. Mais nous n’avons jamais perdu espoir. Nous n’avons jamais perdu la foi. Et face à tout l’argent investi contre nous, et contre toute attente, nous avons repris notre pouvoir. Toujours, toujours parier sur l’outsider. Nous avons bâti un mouvement comme cet État n’en a jamais connu. Nous avons uni des Texans de tous horizons et de toutes convictions au sein d’une même équipe pour affronter ce système politique corrompu et défaillant. Des électeurs qui votaient pour la première fois, des électeurs qui avaient voté trois fois pour Trump, des travailleurs de tous les coins de cet État qui en ont assez, et qui sont prêts pour le changement. Cette victoire, cette victoire est pour tous les outsiders qu’on a donnés perdants et laissés pour compte. Cette victoire est pour chaque enseignant et chaque infirmière et chaque infirmier, pour chaque agriculteur et chaque éleveur, pour chaque jeune qui essaie d’acheter une maison, pour chaque parent qui essaie de nourrir sa famille. Cette victoire, cette victoire est pour tous les Texans qui se sont un jour demandé si quelqu’un les écoutait. Je vous ai entendus. Nous vous avons entendus. Et ce soir, le monde entier vous entend. Aux Texans qui ont soutenu ce mouvement, je suis profondément touché par votre confiance, et je travaillerai chaque jour pour m’en montrer digne. Et aux Texans qui n’ont pas voté pour moi, je serai aussi votre sénateur. Je serai toujours à votre service. Je me battrai toujours pour vous. Cette victoire n’a rien à voir avec le Parti démocrate ou le Parti républicain. Elle dépasse largement cela. Il y a quelque chose qui ne fonctionne plus en Amérique. Notre système économique est défaillant. Notre système politique est défaillant. Même nos relations les uns avec les autres semblent brisées. C’est parce que les personnes les plus puissantes du monde veulent les choses ainsi. Mon grand-père était un prédicateur baptiste du sud du Texas. Et quand j’étais petit, il m’a dit que nous étions les disciples d’un rabbin aux pieds nus qui nous a donné deux commandements : aimer Dieu et aimer son prochain. Parce qu’il n’y a pas d’amour de Dieu sans amour de son prochain. Chaque personne porte en elle l’image du sacré. Chaque personne est sacrée. Pas seulement mon prochain qui me ressemble, pas seulement mon prochain qui prie comme moi, pas seulement mon prochain qui vote comme moi. Je suis appelé à aimer tous mes prochains comme je m’aime moi-même. Car, malgré nos différences, nous voulons tous les mêmes choses : un quartier sûr, un bon emploi, une école publique de qualité et bien financée, et la possibilité de consulter un médecin quand nous en avons besoin. Mais les milliardaires qui possèdent les algorithmes des réseaux sociaux, qui possèdent les chaînes d’information en continu, qui possèdent les politiciens qui se bagarrent sur nos écrans, ils veulent nous monter les uns contre les autres. Ils veulent que nous nous concentrions sur ce qui nous différencie plutôt que sur ce qui nous unit. Ils veulent que nous regardions à gauche et à droite, les uns vers les autres, plutôt que de lever les yeux vers eux. Le véritable combat dans ce pays n’oppose pas la gauche à la droite. Il oppose ceux d’en haut et ceux d’en bas. Ceux qui sont au sommet travaillent d’arrache-pied pour nous maintenir dans la colère et la division, car notre unité menace leur richesse et leur pouvoir. Nous l’avons vu au cours de cette campagne. Nous l’avons vu dans chaque spot de dénigrement financé par des milliardaires. Ceux qui sont au sommet nous divisent par parti, par origine ethnique, par genre, par religion, par culture, pour que l’on ne remarque pas qu’ils nous volent, qu’ils privent nos écoles de financement, qu’ils démantèlent notre système de santé, qu’ils augmentent les impôts pour nous tous, tout en réduisant les leurs. C’est la stratégie la plus ancienne du monde : diviser pour mieux régner. Mais ce soir, nous avons envoyé un message clair comme de l’eau de roche à ceux qui sont au sommet : nous ne nous laisserons pas dominer. Nous ne nous laisserons pas vaincre. Je pense pouvoir affirmer sans me tromper que nous en avons assez d’être montés les uns contre les autres. Nous en avons assez qu’on nous dise de nous détester. Cela fait dix ans que dure ce genre de politique. La politique comme un jeu de massacre. La politique comme provocation et comme humiliation. La politique comme combat de catch. Elle déchire les familles. Elle met fin aux amitiés, et elle nous rend malheureux en permanence. Les gens de tous bords politiques ont soif d’une politique différente. Pas une politique de la haine, pas une politique de la peur, pas une politique de la division, mais une politique de l’amour. Ma foi m’enseigne que l’amour est la force la plus puissante de l’univers. L’amour n’est pas passif. L’amour n’est pas neutre. L’amour n’est pas faible. L’amour exige que nous nous interposions entre les brutes et leurs victimes. L’amour exige que nous regardions le mal droit dans les yeux sans ciller. Ce genre d’amour a toujours été une menace pour les pouvoirs en place. Ce genre d’amour est révolutionnaire. Ce genre d’amour est créatif. La haine est prévisible. La haine est ennuyeuse. La haine ne peut pas réduire nos factures d’énergie. La haine ne peut pas construire un avenir. Mais ce que la haine ne peut pas faire, l’amour le peut. L’amour peut transformer un élève en un érudit. L’amour peut transformer un placard en chambre de bébé. L’amour peut transformer un ennemi en ami. L’amour peut transformer une campagne en un mouvement. L’amour peut réparer ce qui est brisé en Amérique. Nous ne pouvons pas vaincre la politique de la division par davantage de division. À ce jeu, nous ne pouvons pas gagner. Nous devons en changer les règles. D’après mon expérience, lorsque l’on tend une main ouverte, plutôt qu’un poing serré, on est surpris de voir qui la saisit. Nous n’avons pas remporté cette élection en aliénant nos voisins, en les humiliant ou en les ridiculisant. Nous avons incarné un nouveau type de politique, une politique enracinée dans un amour profond pour notre État, pour notre pays et, surtout, pour tous nos prochains. Nous avons mobilisé nos 60 000 bénévoles aux quatre coins de l’État, et ensemble, nous avons distribué des bouteilles d’eau à Sandbranch, une petite localité au sud de Dallas dépourvue d’eau courante. Nous avons fait don de fournitures scolaires à une école primaire d’El Cenizo, une petite ville à la frontière. Nous avons collecté plus de neuf tonnes de nourriture pour les familles de Fort Worth qui peinent à faire face au coût élevé de la vie. Avant de changer à la télévision ou dans les journaux, le monde change d’une personne à l’autre. Chaque fois que l’on choisit d’être bienveillant, à chaque voisin que l’on choisit d’aimer, à chaque prière que l’on dit pour quelqu’un qui ne prierait pas pour nous en retour. C’est comme cela que nous avons remporté le Texas. C’est une victoire aussi grande que le Texas lui-même. Et maintenant, notre mandat est aussi grand que le Texas lui-même. Cette élection portait sur une vision de ce que cet État peut devenir : des écoles publiques texanes qui font l’envie de la nation ; une économie texane sans égale ; et des familles texanes plus fortes et en meilleure santé qu’elles ne l’ont jamais été. Cela ne se fera pas du jour au lendemain, mais un État gigantesque mérite des rêves gigantesques. Et nous savons comment y parvenir. Nous devons chasser l’argent des grands donateurs de la politique afin qu’aucun milliardaire ou trillionnaire ne puisse acheter nos élections. Nous devons défaire le trucage de ce système économique qui ne profite qu’aux 1 % les plus riches. Nous devons adopter une couverture médicale universelle pour que personne ne soit ruiné simplement parce qu’il est tombé malade. Nous devons investir dans nos professeurs et nos élèves afin que chaque outsider ait une chance de s’en sortir. Nous devons mettre un terme à ces guerres corrompues et sans fin qui font grimper les prix et qui tuent les hommes et les femmes courageux de notre armée. Et nous devons guérir la profonde corruption spirituelle qui est à l’origine de toutes ces crises. Nous devons combler les fossés qui nous séparent et réparer les liens qui nous unissent. Nous avons forgé ici, dans l’État de « l’Étoile solitaire », un nouveau type de politique, une réponse à cette décennie de division. Nous avons montré que lorsque les travailleurs s’unissent au-delà de toutes les lignes de fracture, nous pouvons accomplir des choses extraordinaires. Nous avons remporté cette élection afin que ceux qui aspirent au changement le voient enfin advenir. L’ancienne politique se meurt, et une nouvelle politique est en train de naître. Grâce à chacun d’entre nous, grâce à chaque outsider, grâce à chaque David face à chaque Goliath, grâce à chaque Texan qui a cru en notre État et qui a cru en ce mouvement. Le vrai travail commence maintenant. Il y a deux mille ans, quand ceux d’en haut maltraitaient ses prochains, ce rabbin aux pieds nus n’est pas resté dans sa chambre à prier. Il est allé au cœur du pouvoir et il a renversé les tables de l’injustice. Alors que ce mouvement se dirige vers le cœur du pouvoir, alors que nous nous dirigeons vers le Sénat des États-Unis, nous savons ce que ce moment exige de nous. Texas, il est temps de renverser la table. L’article Le démocrate qui a conquis le Texas en opposant « l’amour » à Trump est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Protecting lives and public assets through government vehicle insurance
items.description: Honourable Speaker, I rise to speak on a matter of life, justice and public trust: the continued exemption of government vehicles from compulsory third-party insurance. Mr Speaker, when a family loses a mother, a father or a child on our roads, its grief does not depend on the number plate of the vehicle that caused the loss. A child is no less an orphan because the vehicle was state-owned. The law we make, and the law we exempt Mr. Speaker, the Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Act, 1958 (Act 42) is sixty-eight years old. Section 1 forbids any person to use, or permit the use of, a motor vehicle unless a third-party policy is in force. Breach is an offence, punishable by a fine of up to 250 penalty units, one year’s imprisonment, or both. Nonetheless, the same Act exempts the user of a vehicle owned by, or exclusively employed in the service of, the Government while it is used for Government purposes. We demand of the trader, the taxi driver and the tricycle rider what the State does not demand of itself. The scale of the carnage Mr. Speaker, the National Road Safety Authority reports that 2,949 Ghanaians died in 14,743 road crashes in 2025. That is the highest annual toll in 35 years, up from 2,494 deaths in 2024, a rise of 18.2 per cent. A further 16,714 people were injured, and 2,561 pedestrians were knocked down. Since 1991, road crashes have claimed 63,599 lives. Police MTTD figures, compiled separately, record 2,151 deaths in 10,157 crashes between January and September this year, about eight lives every day. The NRSA estimates that crashes cost the nation more than US$230 million annually, about 1.7 per cent of GDP. The State’s vehicles travel the same roads. Ambulances, school buses, official cars and agency pick-ups are not protected from crashes and do not make exceptions for the people they hit. An exposure we have long known Mr. Speaker, in 2018, a Senior Minister explained that government vehicles were not insured as a matter of policy, because the State was prepared to pay compensation rather than buy cover. In 2022, the Public Accounts Committee’s findings were cited in this House: more than 18,000 government vehicles, with some 98 to 99 per cent uninsured. In July 2024, a GETFund school bus without insurance was involved in a crash near Koforidua, leaving the victims without any insurance benefit. And only this July, the Minister for Health told the Government Assurance Committee that the entire national ambulance fleet was uninsured when he assumed office, leaving the State to bear the full cost of repairs after crashes. I commend the Minister for correcting that. His action proves the principle: insuring state vehicles is practical, and it should not stop at ambulances. Why “the Government will pay” is not a safeguard Mr. Speaker, it is argued that Government can simply self-insure. However, self-insurance without a ring-fenced fund is a promise on paper. The victim must petition a ministry, sue the Attorney-General, and then wait for a budget line that may not exist. The National Insurance Commission has itself said that the processes Ghanaians face to obtain compensation from state-owned vehicles are far from straightforward, and has sought a review of this very exemption. Insurance offers something better. Under Act 42, insurers must satisfy judgments obtained against the insured, and third parties hold enforceable rights against the insurer. Compensation becomes a right, not a favour. For the State, a premium is a known, budgetable cost; an open-ended judgment debt is not. Premiums spread risk, and they bring to public fleets the claims discipline that private fleets already accept. Equality, accountability and confidence Mr. Speaker, Article 17 of our Constitution declares that all persons are equal before the law. A law that binds citizens but excuses the State fails that test. It also weakens confidence in the insurance system itself, because the public will not trust a regime that the State declines to join. When Government insures its fleet, it demonstrates leadership in compliance, and it strengthens the sector it asks citizens to patronise. A non-partisan call to action Mr Speaker, this is not an indictment of one administration. Successive governments, including mine, left this exemption untouched. Fixing it should be a test we all pass. I therefore call on Government to: Bring amendments to Act 42, with the National Insurance Commission and the Attorney-General, to remove the exemption for government vehicles. Direct all Ministries, Departments and Agencies to insure their fleets now, and register them on the Motor Insurance Database, without waiting for the amendment. Provide for the premiums in the 2027 Budget, and publish an audit of the State’s vehicle fleet and its insurance status. Mr. Speaker, a State that asks its citizens to insure must be willing to insure itself. Let us give every victim of a road crash the same assurance of compensation, whoever was at the wheel. Thank you, Mr Speaker. ****** This joint statement was delivered on the Floor of Parliament on November 4, 2026 by Minority Chief Whip, Frank Annoh-Dompreh and Majority Chief Whip, Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor

items.title: Asif says Chaudhry Salik's remarks about corruption in Punjab 'beyond my understanding'
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Wednesday that Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s remarks regarding corruption in Punjab were “beyond my understanding”. During a talk show on a private television channel on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader had lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi . However, he had also criticised the present provincial administration, headed by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption. On Tuesday, CM Maryam had sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to the minister, demanding that he retract his remarks. In a post on the social media platform X on Wednesday, Asif said, “Chaudhry Salik Sahib is very respected in my eyes; I respect his elders just as I respect my own. “His statement regarding corruption in Punjab is beyond my limited political understanding. Corruption is the biggest issue in our society and it is the collective responsibility of the political leadership, both at the central and provincial levels, to rid the country of this curse,” he said. He went on to say that Salik was a part of “both the federal and provincial governments and the leadership of both these governments lies with the PML-N”. “If this statement is part of some future political agenda — to target Maryam Nawaz’s government and carve out space for himself in Punjab and at the Centre to secure his political future — then it starts to make sense,” Asif said. He also praised Maryam’s performance, saying her work across Punjab’s cities and villages and the service standards being set by her government would pose a “very difficult challenge” for its opponents. Meanwhile, Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb sought an apology from Salik over his comments, saying that the PML-Q leader was “himself admitting that he has no evidence to support the allegations he made regarding corruption in the Punjab government”. “After this, what dignity, justice, and principles demand is clear: an apology should be sought for the lack of evidence and for making baseless allegations, rather than turning the transfer of a single DC into an issue of personal ego,” she wrote. The Punjab minister called on Salik to either fulfil his responsibilities as a minister or step down from his role “instead of engaging in empty rhetoric about eradicating corruption from society and promoting good governance”. “We will not tolerate false and baseless allegations against the chief minister who has set an example of serving the people in Pakistan through hard work and transparency in two and a half years,” Aurangzeb asserted. Acknowledging that corruption existed as a “disease in every society in the world”, she contended that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister herself was “leading the campaign to eliminate corruption”. What did Salik say? During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending , particularly the use of official aircraft , arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips. He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance. The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote. While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab. On Tuesday, CM Maryam said the PML-Q leader’s anger stemmed from neither corruption nor progress. She said the issue was that she had changed the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days earlier, whereas Salik wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed. The defamation notice — sent to Salik, ARY News host Naeem Ashraf Butt and the channel’s chairman — said the minister’s remarks were not just an expression of disagreement with policy or “ordinary political criticism”, but conveyed “serious imputations” of widespread corruption in the province. The notice called on them to retract the remarks, publish an “unconditional and unequivocal apology and clarification” and “remove or suitably correct” the portions of the interview in question. It also demanded a sum of Rs5bn in damages. Meanwhile, responding to Maryam’s remarks, Salik said he stood by his statement and had responded honestly to a question during the interview. The minister’s remarks had also drawn a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised Salik not to “bite the hand that feeds him”. Bokhari also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request to appoint a deputy commissioner of his choice being turned down.

items.title: Ghana risks complicity in Sahel terrorism if galamsey persists – Zanetor warns
items.description: Ghana’s failure to decisively tackle illegal mining could expose the country to accusations of complicity in violent extremism and terrorism in the Sahel, the Minister for Environment, Science and Technology, Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings, has warned. She said proceeds from illegal mining were allegedly being used to finance terrorism and violent extremism in parts of the Sahel, warning that Ghana must act to prevent the country from being associated with such activities. “We also know of the fact that a lot of the resources from illegal mining are feeding violent extremism and terrorism in the Sahel,” she said. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings cautioned: “Let it not be said that Ghana has become complicit in violent extremism and terrorism by not handling the canker of illegal mining.” She was speaking at a national conference on small-scale mining for Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) in Kumasi. The Minister also warned that pollution of shared river systems was damaging Ghana’s relations with neighbouring countries. “Earlier this year, concerns over pollution in Tano and Bia rivers raised questions about the movement of contaminated waters across our borders into Côte d’Ivoire. This should remind us that illegal mining is not just an environmental challenge within our jurisdiction. It has implications for our regional relations and national security,” she said. She stressed that Ghana could not afford to take its peace and stability for granted. “It may seem that trouble may never come to Ghana because God has been so gracious to Ghana; let’s not tempt fate, let’s act now,” she added. Dr Agyeman-Rawlings further warned that the destruction of forest reserves and pollution of water bodies through galamsey were undermining food security and exposing future generations to serious health risks. She insisted that the country must not sacrifice agriculture, water security and other vital economic sectors in pursuit of gold. Describing local government as critical to the fight against illegal mining, she said: “Local government is the pillar holding our republic up; when it disintegrates, that will be the end of our democracy.”

items.title: Peter Obi storms Calabar for NDC town hall as supporters throng airport, streets
items.description: By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, on Wednesday arrived in Calabar, the Cross River State capital, ahead of the party’s presidential town hall meeting with stakeholders and supporters, to a rousing reception by party leaders and loyalists. The former Anambra State governor landed at the Margaret Ekpo International Airport, Calabar, in the afternoon, where party faithful had converged to receive him. He was welcomed by top NDC leaders in the state, party stakeholders and a large crowd of supporters who chanted solidarity songs and displayed party flags and banners. From the airport, Obi’s convoy moved through major streets of the Calabar metropolis amid cheers from supporters and residents, a development that caused a brief traffic gridlock along the route. Obi is expected to attend the presidential town hall meeting organised by the NDC at Metropolitan Hotel, Calabar, where he will interact with party members, stakeholders and residents on his plans for the country ahead of the 2027 general election. Security has been beefed up around the venue and other strategic locations in the metropolis.
