items.title: Municipales en Afrique du Sud : l’ANC menacé d’un nouveau recul, sur fond de fragmentation politique
items.description: Les Sud-Africains sont appeles aux urnes ce 4 novembre pour des elections municipales qui ont debute a 7 h, heure locale (5 h GMT). Quelque 29,2 millions d'electeurs sont inscrits sur les listes electorales, repartis entre 23 696 bureaux de vote. Plus de 136 000 candidats sont en lice pour les 10 526 sieges a pourvoir. Le scrutin s'annonce difficile pour le Congres national africain (ANC). Selon plusieurs medias sud-africains, il pourrait se transformer en vote sanction contre le parti au pouvoir, qui domine la vie politique sud-africaine depuis la fin de l'apartheid, en 1994, mais dont le soutien populaire s'est progressivement erode. Les electeurs doivent renouveler les conseils des huit municipalites metropolitaines, des 44 districts et des 205 municipalites locales. Ces assemblees seront ensuite chargees de designer les maires. L'enjeu est d'autant plus important qu'en 2021, l'ANC avait recueilli moins de 50 % des suffrages aux elections municipales pour la premiere fois de son histoire. Le parti a ensuite perdu sa majorite parlementaire lors des elections generales de 2024, le contraignant a former un gouvernement de coalition avec l'Alliance democratique (DA) et plusieurs autres formations. a l'approche du scrutin, certaines enquetes d'opinion laissaient entrevoir un nouveau recul de l'ANC, dont le score pourrait passer sous la barre des 40 %. Cyril Ramaphosa reconnaît des defaillances S'exprimant apres avoir vote au lycee Hyde Park de Johannesburg, le president sud-africain Cyril Ramaphosa a reconnu les difficultes persistantes auxquelles sont confrontees les municipalites du pays dans la fourniture des services publics. Le chef de l'etat a notamment evoque les penuries d'eau, les defaillances dans la collecte des dechets et les perturbations des services essentiels, admettant que les administrations locales devaient redoubler d'efforts pour repondre aux attentes de la population. Cyril Ramaphosa a egalement reaffirme la determination de son gouvernement a reformer l'administration locale et a ameliorer le fonctionnement des municipalites. Il s'est dit convaincu que le scrutin permettrait l'election de conseillers davantage engages au service des citoyens, independamment de leur appartenance politique. Il a ainsi appele les futurs elus a prendre pleinement conscience de leurs responsabilites envers les populations qu'ils representent et a inaugurer une nouvelle approche de la gouvernance municipale. Majorite absolue hors de portee ? L'erosion du soutien a l'ANC pourrait accentuer la fragmentation du paysage politique sud-africain et favoriser la multiplication des alliances et des gouvernements locaux de coalition. Selon une etude de l'Institut Mapungubwe de reflexion strategique (MISTRA), 74 municipalites etaient dirigees par des coalitions ou des administrations minoritaires en fevrier 2026, temoignant de la recomposition progressive des equilibres politiques locaux. Le taux de participation constitue un autre enjeu majeur. Lors des municipales de 2021, seuls 46 % environ des electeurs inscrits s'etaient rendus aux urnes, un niveau historiquement bas. Pour les observateurs, les resultats du scrutin permettront de mesurer les nouveaux rapports de force entre les principales formations politiques et de degager les tendances susceptibles de peser sur les elections nationales et provinciales de 2029. Le depouillement doit debuter des la fermeture des bureaux de vote, prevue a 21 h. Les premiers resultats seront communiques progressivement, au rythme de l'avancement des operations de comptage.

items.title: Soludo has awarded 908km of roads since 2022 — Commissioner
items.description: …Ezeobi says 442km asphalted, less than 5km affected by failures By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has awarded contracts for the construction of 908.44 kilometres of roads across the state since Governor Chukwuma Soludo assumed office in 2022, the Commissioner for Works, Architect Okey Ezeobi, has said. Ezeobi, who disclosed this while addressing journalists in Awka, said 442 kilometres of the roads had been fully asphalted, describing the administration’s road construction programme as unprecedented in the state’s history. He claimed that the combined road construction achievements of the three previous governors fell short of the number of kilometres asphalted by the Soludo administration. According to him, the government has awarded 143 road contracts since taking office. Addressing complaints on social media about the condition of some roads constructed by the administration, the commissioner said the affected portions amounted to less than five kilometres out of the 442 kilometres asphalted. “Of all the 442 kilometres of road we have asphalted, if you cut the portions that failed as a result of the effects of underground water, they are not up to five kilometres. That means that we have over 95 per cent of all the roads constructed by this administration in perfect condition,” he said. Ezeobi attributed some of the reported road failures to underground water, unusually heavy rainfall and blocked drainage channels, insisting that the government was addressing the affected sections. He alleged that some residents deliberately blocked drainage channels to allow sand to accumulate for harvesting and commercial sale, thereby worsening flooding and damaging public infrastructure. The commissioner explained that some roads remained in good condition until the recent heavy rainy season, which he said exposed the effects of underground water that had not been adequately captured in the initial construction data. “Many of the roads were designed and built and they never became bad until this year’s heavy rainy season. It’s the underground water that is the cause of the road damage, as the data we used did not capture the volume of the underground water,” he said. He added that the effects of underground water were also visible in residential buildings, where ground-floor surfaces were reportedly peeling. On allegations of poor construction standards and the engagement of unqualified contractors, Ezeobi maintained that the government had carefully selected reputable construction firms to handle its projects. He described the contractors as A-rated companies, saying they had the capacity to return to sites and carry out reconstruction whenever defects occurred. According to him, the affected contractors were undertaking the repairs at no additional cost to the state government. He, however, acknowledged that human errors could not be completely ruled out as a possible cause of some road failures. The commissioner cited the Amawbia-Ekwulobia dual carriageway as one of the roads facing challenges because of erosion-prone sections and swampy areas where underground water frequently rises. He said the volume of rainfall recorded this year was unprecedented in the past 50 years, adding that floodwater had seeped underground and affected road infrastructure, including some Federal Government projects. Ezeobi disclosed that the government planned to remove damaged asphalt in affected areas and undertake cement-based stabilisation to prevent further damage from underground water. He said the process would begin after the underground water had sufficiently drained, after which the stabilised sections would be allowed to set before fresh asphalt was applied. The commissioner assured residents that the government remained committed to delivering quality roads, adding that the ongoing reconstruction was deliberate and would not attract additional costs to the state. He dismissed some social media criticisms of the state’s road projects as politically motivated, arguing that the comments did not reflect the actual situation on the ground. Ezeobi said the government would formally announce the completion and certification of the affected roads before their official reopening to motorists. He added that the administration was working to ensure that roads across the state were motorable before the Christmas season. Nigerian footballer hospitalised after head kick in Spain
items.description: Nigerian midfielder Quadri Liameed was knocked unconscious after being kicked in the head during a Spanish second-division match between his club, Sabadell, and Albacete. The 24-year-old suffered the injury in the 42nd minute of the encounter at the Carlos Belmonte Stadium on Saturday. The incident occurred when Albacete forward José Corpas attempted a volley but struck Liameed in the head as both players challenged for the ball. A viral video sighted by PUNCH Online on Wednesday shows the moment the midfielder took the hard hit right outside the box. Liameed collapsed on the pitch and briefly lost consciousness, prompting medical personnel from both clubs to rush to his aid. He was fitted with a neck brace, carried off on a stretcher and taken by ambulance to Hospital Quirón Santa Cristina for medical examination. The moment Liameed was carried off on a stretcher and taken by ambulance to Hospital Quirón Santa Cristina for medical examination. CREDIT: Tribuna As reported by Tribuna on Sunday, Corpas was shown a straight red card for the challenge, while the match was stopped for about nine minutes. Sabadell later confirmed that Liameed was conscious and undergoing medical examinations, with the initial test results described as positive. In an update posted on its X handle on November 1, the club announced that the Nigerian had been discharged from hospital after the medical tests returned positive results. “The best of the news has arrived! “@Qlimeed has received medical discharge after all the tests have come out well and will return tonight to Sabadell! “We want to thank the medical services of @AlbaceteBPSAD for the help received at all times,” the club said. The former Nigeria U-20 midfielder subsequently returned to Sabadell by car, accompanied by a member of the club’s medical staff. Credit: X | Smolarek__ — Follow us for more breaking news and videos https://t.co/mHY2OHEz6g — Punch Newspapers (@MobilePunch) November 4, 2026 As reported by Bsnsports on Tuesday, Liameed’s father, Hajji Gafar, confirmed his condition saying, “My son is now in a stable condition and is expected to undergo a Buffalo Concussion Bike Test (BCBT) within the next 48 hours. The Spanish medical team attending to him gave me some encouraging news yesterday, and I am relieved and grateful. “I also intend to travel to Spain within the next 10 days to personally see Quadri, spend some time with him and support him through this recovery process.” Despite the incident, Albacete secured a 2-1 victory over Sabadell, having played with 10 men following Corpas’s dismissal. Born in Lagos on April 8, 2002, Liameed began his football career with Lagos-based 36 Lion FC before moving to Spain. He later played for Lleida Esportiu before joining Sabadell in July 2025. According to Tribuna, Corpas could face a ban of between four and 12 matches under Article 102 of the Spanish football disciplinary code if the incident is deemed to have caused serious injury. The punishment is yet to be determined by the Spanish Football Federation’s Disciplinary Committee.

items.title: Russie – Ukraine : une guerre sans fin ? Avec Arnaud Dubien
items.description: Alors que la guerre en Ukraine se poursuit depuis maintenant près de quatre ans, une nouvelle séquence diplomatique est sur le point de s’ouvrir. Des délégations russes, ukrainiennes et états-uniennes sont attendues le 10 et 11 novembre à Abu Dhabi. Cette initiative évince de fait les Européens qui peinent une fois de plus à s’affirmer dans les discussions sur la fin du conflit. Alors qu’elle assume déjà un soutien budgétaire massif à l’Ukraine depuis le début de l’invasion, l’Union européenne risque de se voir contrainte d’assumer seule le fardeau logistique et financier de la reconstruction de l’Ukraine dans les années à venir. La ligne de front n’est en effet pas la seule zone à subir de plein fouet la guerre. Le conflit se joue en désormais parfois très loin de celle-ci, en raison de la multiplication des frappes de longues portées visant les infrastructures stratégiques, notamment liées à l’énergie, l’industrie et aux transports. Dans cette guerre d’attrition, qui teste les capacités de résiliences des deux belligérants, aucune issue claire ne semble encore se dégager. L’Union européenne se trouve-t-elle dans une impasse ? Quels sont les objectifs de Vladimir Poutine ? Quelle est la stratégie de Volodymyr Zelensky ? La Russie s’est-elle affaiblie depuis 2022 ? Comment la Russie résiste-t-elle aux sanctions économiques ? Que pensent les Russes de la guerre ? Autant d'enjeux abordés avec Arnaud Dubien, chercheur associé à l’IRIS et directeur de l’Observatoire franco-russe. L’article Russie – Ukraine : une guerre sans fin ? Avec Arnaud Dubien est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: GSE annual return hits 63%, listed firms’ Q3 performance impressive
items.description: The Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE) continued its impressive performance in 2026 as the GSE Composite Index (GSE-CI) rose by 1.4% week-on-week to settle at 14,303.4 points last week. This lifted the year-to-date gain to 63.1%, while the 30-day performance turned flat after erasing earlier losses. The index advance was driven by gains in Telecom, Banking and Consumer sector stocks. Aggregate market turnover rose by 2.3% week-on-week(w/w) to US$4.8 million, with Scancom Plc (MTN GH) driving activity and contributing 81.6% of the total value traded. Market breadth leaned negative at a 9:3 ratio in favour of decliners, although gains in high-weighted stocks supported the index. GCB Bank Plc (+4.6% w/w | GH¢42.08) led the gainers’ chart, while Société Générale Ghana (- 7.4% w/w | GH¢4.63) was the worst laggard. Fan Milk’s 9M2026 profit after tax surged 308.9% year-on-year to GH¢173.3mn, driven by 30.2% revenue growth and a 14.1% decline in cost of sales, which lifted gross margin by 22.2 percentage points to 57.0%. Unilever Ghana’s profit after tax rose 205.4% year-on-year to GHS 180.6 million on 18.6% revenue growth and lower input costs, although marketing expenditure rose 58.1%. Kasapreko’s profit after tax grew 14.3% year-on-year to GH¢295.8 million, as higher costs squeezed gross margin by 1.2 percentage points to 29.7%. TotalEnergies’ profit after tax fell by 16.1% year-on-year to GH¢221.8mn, as revenue declined 18.1% on weaker sales volumes. IC Insights expects the nine-month 2026 results to drive stock-specific repricing as investors reassess earnings performance, margin trends and growth prospects across the market.

items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a clôturé en nette hausse mercredi, son indice principal, le MASI, gagnant 2,25% à 16.760,33 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a pris 2,1% à 1.222,07 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody’s ESG Solutions, a avancé de 2,29% à 1.285,84 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a, quant à lui, progressé de 1,24% à 1.578,24 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Mines » (+4,91%), « Sociétés de portefeuilles – Holdings » (+4,36%) et « Distributeurs » (+4,15%) ont signé les meilleures performances. Le volume global des échanges s’est établi à plus de 328,9 millions de dirhams (MDH), dominés par les transactions sur AtlantaSanad (35,92 MDH), CMGP Group (33,75 MDH) et Addoha (26,75 MDH). La capitalisation boursière a, quant à elle, dépassé 984,73 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, Label Vie (+5,24% à 3.894 DH), Managem (+5,11% à 1.440 DH), SGTM (+4,58% à 548 DH), Salafin (+4,49% à 419 DH) et Delta Holding (+4,41% à 45 DH) réalisaient les meilleures performances. À l’inverse, Lesieur Cristal (-6,01% à 280,1 DH), Maroc Leasing (-5,97% à 338,5 DH), CTM (-4% à 768 DH), Microdata (-2,44% à 760 DH) et Réalisations Mécaniques (-2% à 440 DH) accusaient les plus fortes baisses. items.title: Tambuwal accuses APC of failing Nigerians
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Former Sokoto State Governor, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of failing Nigerians, citing worsening poverty, hunger and insecurity across the country. Tambuwal made the allegations at the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he urged Nigerians to support the opposition party as an alternative to the ruling APC. Addressing party supporters at the rally, the former governor said the APC had failed to provide the leadership needed to address the country’s economic and security challenges. He argued that millions of Nigerians were grappling with worsening economic difficulties, widespread hunger and persistent insecurity, which he said had exposed the ruling party’s inability to govern effectively. Tambuwal maintained that Nigerians deserved a government capable of guaranteeing security, economic stability and better living conditions. He urged citizens to embrace the ADC, describing the party as an alternative capable of addressing the country’s pressing challenges. The former governor’s remarks came amid intensifying political exchanges ahead of the 2027 general elections. He called on Nigerians to rally behind the ADC and its presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, to change the country’s political direction. items.title: PSC dismisses three senior police officers, demotes 16
items.description: …21 others receive severe reprimands, three exonerated By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the dismissal of three senior police officers and the demotion of 16 others over various cases of misconduct. The commission also approved severe reprimands for 21 officers and ordinary reprimands for two others, bringing the number of officers sanctioned to 42. However, three officers were exonerated, while some previously suspended officers were reinstated into the Nigeria Police Force. The decisions were reached at the commission’s plenary meeting presided over by its Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (retd.), at the Solomon Arase Conference Hall, the commission’s corporate headquarters in Abuja. A statement by the PSC spokesman, Torty Njoku, said the disciplinary actions followed established cases of serious misconduct and conduct unbecoming of officers of the law. Reaffirming the commission’s zero tolerance for corruption, human rights abuses, interference in land and civil matters, and other forms of misconduct in the police force, Argungu assured Nigerians that disciplinary cases before the commission would continue to receive speedy attention. The chairman commended the Chairman of the PSC Standing Committee on Discipline and Legal Matters, Justice Paul Adamu Galumje (retd.), and other board members for their contributions to the consideration of the disciplinary cases and appeals. Those commended included DIG (Dr) Taiwo Lakanu (retd.), Justice Christine Dabup, Alhaji Abdulfatah Mohammed, the Secretary to the Commission, Chief Onyemuche Nnamani, and the Director of the Police Discipline Department, Mr Ferdinand U. Ekpe. Argungu acknowledged their dedication throughout the departmental, committee and plenary consideration of the cases. items.title: Senate proposes six-month jail term for hospitals denying emergency care
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has passed for second reading a bill seeking to make it compulsory for public and private hospitals across Nigeria to provide emergency medical treatment, prescribing up to six months’ imprisonment for facilities and individuals who violate its provisions. The proposed legislation also prescribes a fine of up to ₦300,000, imprisonment for six months, or both, for anyone convicted of denying emergency medical treatment. The bill, sponsored by Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’Adua (APC, Katsina Central), seeks to amend the National Health Act, 2014, to establish mandatory emergency medical treatment standards and referral protocols in healthcare facilities. Titled, “A Bill for an Act to Amend the National Health Act, 2014 to Provide for Emergency Medical Treatment Standards and Referral Protocols in Healthcare Facilities; and for Related Matters, 2026” (SB. 759), it was referred to the Senate Committee on Health (Secondary and Tertiary) for further legislative action, with a directive to report back in four weeks. Under the proposed amendment, no healthcare provider, health worker or medical establishment would be allowed to deny anyone emergency medical treatment for any reason. It also requires healthcare professionals to commence life-saving interventions, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, airway management and bleeding control, immediately after identifying a life-threatening condition. The bill proposes that hospitals conduct triage and initial assessments within 15 minutes of a patient’s arrival, while basic stabilisation measures, including oxygen administration, intravenous fluids, pain management and initial diagnostic procedures, must begin within 30 minutes. For patients requiring admission, hospital beds are to be assigned within two hours, subject to availability. Where beds are unavailable, healthcare facilities would be required to commence immediate stabilisation and arrange the patient’s transfer to another hospital. The proposed legislation further requires hospitals to initiate referral arrangements within two hours and complete the transfer process within three hours of a patient’s arrival, except where circumstances beyond their control prevent compliance. It also mandates hospitals to dispatch an ambulance or arrange alternative transportation within 30 minutes of communicating a referral decision. Beyond emergency response timelines, the bill seeks to introduce mandatory emergency care training and certification for healthcare workers, with recertification intervals not exceeding 18 months. It also mandates the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria to jointly develop a standardised national emergency care curriculum. However, healthcare practitioners would be protected from penalties where resource constraints prevent compliance, provided the challenges are properly documented and prescribed referral procedures are followed. Leading debate on the bill, Yar’Adua said the proposed amendment would address critical gaps in Nigeria’s healthcare system by establishing enforceable standards for emergency treatment and referral procedures. He said it would guarantee timely and life-saving medical attention to Nigerians during emergencies, irrespective of their social status, wealth, influence or location. According to him, preventable deaths persist because many healthcare facilities lack clearly defined and enforceable timelines for patient assessment, stabilisation and treatment. He cited Nigeria’s contribution to approximately 10 per cent of global maternal deaths, attributing part of the problem to delays in accessing emergency obstetric care. Yar’Adua said the proposed legislation would strengthen coordination among primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare facilities, while ensuring that patients are stabilised before being referred to other hospitals. He added that the bill would protect healthcare workers acting in good faith within documented resource limitations while ensuring accountability for wilful negligence. The senator said the proposed amendment was consistent with international practices, citing Ghana, South Africa, Kenya, the United Kingdom and the United States. Supporting the bill, the Senate Whip, Senator Mohammed Monguno (APC, Borno North), said it would address deaths arising from road accidents and maternal emergencies. He lamented that some healthcare providers neglected emergency patients, resulting in avoidable deaths, and said the proposed amendment would introduce criminal liability for such negligence. Monguno said the legislation would address gaps in the existing National Health Act and reinforce government’s responsibility to protect the welfare of citizens. Similarly, Senator Diket Plang (Plateau Central) said the bill would improve emergency admissions and establish appropriate referral procedures across different levels of healthcare delivery. He noted that rural communities particularly needed the intervention because childbirth complications often required urgent referrals from primary healthcare centres to higher-level facilities. Plang stressed that patients must be stabilised before transportation, adding that the proposed provisions would help prevent avoidable deaths during emergency transfers. However, Senator Francis Faduyile (APC, Ondo South) cautioned against criminalising healthcare professionals without first addressing inadequate facilities, personnel shortages and other systemic challenges. He said many hospitals lacked sufficient doctors, oxygen cylinders and emergency equipment, making it difficult for healthcare workers to meet the proposed timelines. Faduyile questioned how a doctor attending to several patients simultaneously could be held criminally responsible when another emergency case arrived. He also raised concerns about inadequate funding, noting that private healthcare providers frequently attended to emergency patients without receiving reimbursement for the services. The senator argued that Nigeria’s healthcare challenges required a comprehensive review of the National Health Act rather than concentrating solely on sanctions against healthcare professionals. The Senate Minority Leader, Senator Abba Moro (PDP, Benue South), said the bill had exposed several gaps requiring comprehensive legislative attention. He expressed confidence that the committee stage and proposed public hearing would provide opportunities for healthcare professionals and other stakeholders to make contributions. Moro, who cited experiences in Mexico where emergency responders and ambulances reportedly attended promptly to accident victims, condemned the practice of hospitals demanding police reports before treating emergency patients. He stressed that saving lives should remain the priority in emergency situations. In his remarks, the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, said the debate had highlighted important challenges requiring attention across the country’s healthcare system. Akpabio urged lawmakers to support the bill’s progression, noting that identified shortcomings could be addressed through further legislative deliberations and consultations with relevant stakeholders. He stressed that the Federal Government, state governments and local government authorities must work together to provide the facilities and resources required for effective healthcare delivery. items.title: Putin’s reported commitment is a diplomatic win for Ghana – but the fight to protect our citizens is not over
items.description: When Ghana’s name was mentioned at the United Nations over allegations that its citizens were being recruited to fight in Russia’s war against Ukraine, the country could not afford to look the other way. Our citizens deserved protection, our government owed the nation answers, and the world deserved to know where Ghana stood. Today, following President John Dramani Mahama’s engagement with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Ghana’s Foreign Affairs Minister says Moscow has agreed to halt the recruitment of Ghanaians. This is welcome news. But the bigger question remains: “Will this commitment translate into lasting protection for Ghanaian lives?” The reported commitment by Russian President Vladimir Putin to halt the recruitment of Ghanaians to fight in the ongoing Russia-Ukraine conflict is a significant diplomatic development that deserves national attention. According to a statement by Ghana’s Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, President Putin committed to this following discussions with President John Dramani Mahama on the sidelines of the recently concluded Russia-Africa Summit. The announcement, first reported by GhanaWeb, represents an important development in Ghana’s efforts to address concerns about the involvement of its citizens in a foreign war. It also brings renewed attention to an issue that should never have been treated as a distant international controversy. Ghana was mentioned at the United Nations. Why were we not talking about it? When Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed the United Nations General Assembly, he raised concerns about the alleged recruitment of citizens from Ghana and other countries to fight on Russia’s side in the war against Ukraine. He called on President Mahama and the governments concerned to take responsibility for protecting their citizens. That was a serious diplomatic allegation involving Ghana’s national image, the safety of its citizens and the responsibility of the state to protect its people wherever they may be. Yet, following that public accusation, I was concerned by the apparent absence of a sufficiently clear and direct public response from Ghana’s leadership. I therefore took the matter to the public through an article published across media platforms, asking a question I believed every concerned Ghanaian had the right to ask. “ Mr President, Ghana was mentioned at the U.N. Why aren’t we talking about it?” In that article, published by MyJoyOnline, I challenged the government to address the matter and explain what steps were being taken to establish the facts and protect Ghanaians who might be caught up in the conflict. Read my earlier article here: https://www.myjoyonline.com/mr-president-ghana-was-mentioned-at-the-un-why-arent-we-talking-about-it/ I expected that the issue would receive the attention it deserved, particularly when news emerged that President Mahama was travelling to Russia for the Russia-Africa Summit, where an opportunity for direct diplomatic engagement with President Putin presented itself. It was therefore encouraging to hear that the matter was raised and that the Foreign Affairs Minister subsequently announced a commitment from the Russian leader to stop the recruitment of Ghanaians. A diplomatic commitment must become practical protection While this development deserves commendation, Ghanaians must not confuse a diplomatic assurance with the complete resolution of the problem. The government must now provide further clarity on how the commitment will be implemented, monitored and enforced. What mechanisms will prevent Ghanaian citizens from being recruited through unofficial channels, deceptive employment arrangements or intermediaries? What support will be available to Ghanaians who may already have been recruited or find themselves in the conflict zone? How will families seeking information about missing or affected relatives receive assistance? These are not unnecessary questions. They are legitimate concerns arising from the government’s fundamental responsibility to protect its citizens. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs must also strengthen public education, provide reliable channels for reporting suspicious recruitment activities and work with relevant diplomatic partners to identify and assist affected Ghanaians. Above all, the government must ensure that no Ghanaian is misled into believing that an attractive employment opportunity abroad is worth risking their life in a foreign conflict. A salute to citizen journalists, bloggers and professional journalists I also want to use this opportunity to congratulate fellow citizen journalists, social media bloggers, content creators and professional journalists who helped bring this matter into the national conversation and sustained public attention until the government responded. This is a moment worth reflecting on. For too long, some have been quick to dismiss social media journalism and citizen-led reporting as unprofessional or irrelevant. Admittedly, social media can be abused through misinformation, personal attacks, insults and sensationalism. But when used responsibly, it can become a powerful instrument for public accountability. The lesson here is that journalism is not defined merely by the platform on which a story appears. It is defined by the principles guiding the work: accuracy, fairness, verification, responsibility and the courage to ask difficult questions. When citizen journalists, bloggers, content creators and professional journalists work within these principles, they can help expose injustices, challenge institutional silence and demand accountability from those entrusted with public office. This development should remind us that responsible journalism does not have to insult anyone to make an impact. It does not have to descend into political propaganda to demand answers. A well-researched question, presented professionally and supported by facts, can be powerful enough to compel public attention. Ghanaian lives must always come first I welcome the announcement by the Foreign Affairs Minister and commend President Mahama for raising this matter during his engagement with President Putin. However, the ultimate measure of this diplomatic engagement will not be the announcement itself. It will be whether Ghanaian citizens are genuinely protected from recruitment into a war that is not theirs to fight. Our national interest must never be sacrificed on the altar of international politics. Ghanaian lives are precious, whether at home or abroad. And to my fellow journalists and citizen reporters, let us continue to ask the difficult questions, hold public officials accountable and defend the public interest, not through insults, but through facts, professionalism and responsible journalism. Because when the government is silent, responsible journalism must keep asking. And when citizens are at risk, the nation must never look away.

items.title: Nigeria-Korea trade hits $1.1bn as both countries seek diversification
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Republic of Korea has expressed its readiness to deepen trade and investment ties with Nigeria, targeting sectors such as manufacturing, agriculture, digital technology and maritime services beyond the traditional oil and gas trade. The Korean Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yo-an, disclosed this on Wednesday at a meeting with journalists in Abuja, saying expanding economic cooperation would boost bilateral trade, encourage local production and create employment opportunities in both countries. He said trade between Nigeria and Korea reached approximately $1.1bn last year, making Nigeria one of Korea’s largest trading partners in Africa. However, the ambassador noted that the existing trade structure, largely dominated by Nigerian oil and gas exports and Korean exports of automobiles, electronics and machinery, needed to become more diversified. “Last year, our trade reached about 1.1 billion dollars. Nigeria remains one of Korea’s largest trading partners in Africa. But the shape of our trade must change. Today, Nigeria sells us mostly oil and gas. Korea sells mostly cars, electronics and machinery. We can do much more than that,” he said. Jeong said the next phase of bilateral cooperation would focus on strengthening local production, including vehicle assembly, agricultural machinery for rice farmers, digital skills development and maritime services. He added that Korea was interested in encouraging more Nigerian businesses to participate in bilateral trade while attracting Korean companies to invest in local manufacturing and other productive sectors. The ambassador identified the beauty and cosmetics industry as another area offering significant opportunities, citing growing Nigerian interest in Korean skincare and cosmetic products. According to him, Nigeria’s large youth population presents a considerable market for Korean beauty products and could position the country as a major destination for such products in Africa. He said the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), through its Lagos office, was available to connect Korean manufacturers with Nigerian importers and help local businesses identify potential buyers in Korea. Jeong also disclosed that Nigerian buyers would have the opportunity to engage with Korean companies at the Korean pavilion during the Beauty West Africa exhibition scheduled for November 13. On diplomatic relations, he said both countries were working to strengthen political and economic cooperation following the Korea-Africa Summit in 2024 and the first Korea-Africa Foreign Ministers’ Meeting held in June this year. He added that Nigeria had offered to host the seventh session of the Nigeria-Korea Joint Commission in Abuja as part of efforts to advance bilateral engagement. On development cooperation, the ambassador disclosed that approximately 2,000 Nigerian public officials had received training in Korea through the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA). He said KOICA’s Smart School project had also reached 8,000 pupils and trained more than 300 teachers and school leaders. According to him, KOICA, the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) had commenced work on the Abuja Centre for Entrepreneurship to support young Nigerians in developing business ideas and creating jobs. He said Korea was equally supporting initiatives aimed at promoting green jobs, agricultural development, digital education and skills acquisition. The ambassador further disclosed that Korea was working towards increasing its Official Development Assistance to $10bn by 2030, alongside plans to provide $14bn in export financing to support Korean companies investing in Africa. On cultural exchanges, Jeong said the Korean Cultural Centre Nigeria had reached more than 300,000 people through its programmes, while this year’s Korean Film Festival attracted approximately 1,000 participants. He pledged to extend cultural activities to more Nigerian cities and promote collaborations between young creatives in both countries. The post Nigeria-Korea trade hits $1.1bn as both countries seek diversification appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CAN 2027 : Ouahbi veut élargir ses options et donner leur chance aux jeunes face au Niger
items.description: À l’occasion de la double confrontation contre le Niger dans le cadre des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, Mohamed Ouahbi a dévoilé une liste qui mêle retours, nouveaux visages et choix liés à la forme du moment. En conférence de presse, le sélectionneur des Lions de l’Atlas a détaillé sa stratégie : assurer la qualification tout en profitant de ce rassemblement pour tester de nouvelles solutions et préparer progressivement le groupe qui défendra les couleurs du Maroc lors de la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des nations. Ces deux confrontations, comptant pour les 3e et 4e journées des éliminatoires de la Coupe d’Afrique des Nations (CAN 2027), sont programmées les 13 et 17 novembre prochains, à 20h. A cette occasion, le technicien marocain a tenu à faire le point, affichant des ambitions claires : « L’objectif prioritaire reste quand même de nous qualifier, on doit gagner les deux matchs ». Mais cette exigence de résultat n’empêche pas une réflexion à plus long terme. Ouahbi considère cette période comme une occasion importante de donner du temps de jeu à de nouveaux joueurs et d'assurer davantage de continuité à certains jeunes déjà intégrés au groupe. Le sélectionneur souhaite notamment arriver au prochain rassemblement de mars avec une sélection aussi proche que possible de celle appelée à disputer la CAN. « S’il y a bien une période ou un stage où on peut essayer de nouvelles choses ou de nouveaux joueurs, donner de l’opportunité à des nouveaux joueurs, c’est le bon moment » , a-t-il expliqué. Ayoub Oufkir, première convocation et plusieurs retours Parmi les principales nouveautés de cette liste figure Ayoub Oufkir, sociétaire d'AZ Alkmaar, qui connaît sa première convocation avec la sélection A. Le jeune joueur de 20 ans rejoint un groupe dans lequel le staff souhaite intégrer des profils capables d'apporter des solutions à court, moyen et long terme. Ouahbi a également insisté sur la polyvalence de plusieurs jeunes éléments, notamment Abdellah Ouazane et Bilal Khannous, capables d'évoluer à différents postes offensifs. L'objectif est de leur permettre de s'adapter aux exigences de la sélection et de renforcer les possibilités tactiques de l'équipe. La liste est aussi marquée par plusieurs retours, notamment ceux de Youssef En-Nesyri, Reda Belahyane, Souffian El Karouani et Amine Sbaï. Le retour d'En-Nesyri constitue notamment une option supplémentaire en attaque. Ouahbi a expliqué que l'avant-centre possède un profil différent de celui d'Ayoub El Kaabi, privilégié lors de la Coupe du monde, et qu'il peut apporter une présence importante dans la surface. « On connaît ses qualités, on sait ce qu'il peut apporter à l'équipe nationale » , a déclaré le sélectionneur, estimant que le moment était venu de lui redonner l'opportunité de s'exprimer dans son projet de jeu. Les blessures obligent le staff à explorer de nouvelles solutions Le rassemblement intervient également dans un contexte marqué par plusieurs indisponibilités. Ismaël Saibari, Azzedine Ounahi, Ayoub El Kaabi, Soufiane Rahimi, Chadi Riad et Hamza Igamane sont annoncés indisponibles. Interrogé sur la situation des joueurs blessés, Ouahbi a expliqué rester en contact avec eux et suivre leur rééducation. Sans avancer de calendrier précis, il a indiqué que plusieurs pourraient retrouver les terrains d'ici le mois de mars, tout en rappelant que les délais de récupération restent difficiles à déterminer. © Mounir Mehimdate Pour le sélectionneur, ces absences peuvent aussi permettre à d'autres joueurs de se montrer et d'augmenter la concurrence au sein du groupe. « Chaque problème a des solutions » , a-t-il affirmé, ajoutant que ces opportunités pourraient rendre la sélection plus forte à l'avenir. Concernant le poste de numéro 10, Ouahbi n'exclut pas de repositionner Brahim Diaz derrière l'attaquant. Il a toutefois précisé ne pas avoir arrêté de choix particulier, rappelant que Bilal Khannous, Abdellah Ouazane et Amine Sbaï peuvent également occuper ce rôle. « Si je vois que Brahim peut être performant en 10, il jouera en 10 », a-t-il dit. Le technicien a par ailleurs défendu certains choix de sélection, notamment celui de maintenir sa confiance à des joueurs comme Noussair Mazraoui, même lorsque leur temps de jeu en club est limité. Selon lui, les convocations ne reposent pas uniquement sur les statistiques ou le temps passé sur le terrain, mais aussi sur les profils, les qualités individuelles et la capacité à renforcer le collectif. Une concurrence ouverte avant la CAN Mohamed Ouahbi a également tenu à souligner que la porte de la sélection reste ouverte. Le staff suit chaque semaine plus de 60 joueurs, avec l'appui de quatre analystes, afin d'évaluer leurs performances en club. Les joueurs peuvent ainsi intégrer le groupe à condition de répondre aux attentes du staff et de démontrer leur capacité à s'inscrire dans le modèle de jeu de l'équipe nationale. Le sélectionneur a notamment évoqué le cas de Reda Belahyane, dont il apprécie les performances cette saison. Il a également rappelé que les absences de certains joueurs ne signifient pas qu'ils sont écartés durablement de ses plans. Les choix actuels répondent notamment à la volonté de travailler avec un groupe plus réduit. Autre sujet abordé : le retour de la sélection à Casablanca. Ouahbi a expliqué que cette rencontre répondait à une volonté de permettre aux supporters de différentes régions du Royaume de suivre les Lions de l'Atlas de près. Il s'attend à un accueil chaleureux du public et estime que les joueurs devront lui rendre ce soutien sur le terrain. © Mounir Mehimdate Enfin, le sélectionneur a salué les nombreuses nominations marocaines aux CAF Awards 2026, notamment celles d'Achraf Hakimi, Brahim Díaz et Ismaël Saibari pour le titre de meilleur joueur africain, ainsi que celles de plusieurs autres représentants marocains dans différentes catégories. Il a exprimé sa fierté face à cette reconnaissance du football national. À travers ce rassemblement, Mohamed Ouahbi poursuit donc un double objectif : décrocher les résultats nécessaires face au Niger et affiner progressivement son groupe en vue de la CAN 2027. Mais le message du sélectionneur est clair : les opportunités seront nombreuses, à condition que chaque joueur démontre, pendant le stage et sur le terrain, qu'il mérite sa place. The post CAN 2027 : Ouahbi veut élargir ses options et donner leur chance aux jeunes face au Niger appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: «La Russie n’a jamais menacé personne et ne menace personne», affirme Poutine, appelant les États à privilégier la coopération plutôt que la confrontation
items.description: Vladimir Poutine a reaffirme, le 4 novembre au Kremlin, que la Russie n'avait jamais menace personne et cherchait a developper la cooperation avec les autres etats. Le president russe s'exprimait lors d'une ceremonie de remise de distinctions d'etat et de prix consacree aux contributions au renforcement de l'unite nationale. « La Russie n'a jamais menace personne et ne menace personne. Nous cherchons a cooperer », a-t-il declare. Le chef de l'etat a insiste sur la necessite de faire connaître cette position au-dela des frontieres russes, aussi bien aupres des populations que des dirigeants politiques. Il a exprime l'espoir que les pays qui ne sont pas encore prets a cooperer avec Moscou reconsiderent leur attitude et renoncent a privilegier la confrontation. Vladimir Poutine a notamment evoque l'exemple des partenaires etrangers qui entretiennent deja des relations avec la Russie. Il a souhaite que ces experiences encouragent d'autres etats a revoir leur approche et a s'orienter vers une cooperation avec Moscou. Le dialogue culturel et economique, un fondement des relations entre etats Le president russe a egalement souligne le role des echanges culturels, educatifs, humanitaires et economiques dans le developpement des relations internationales. Selon lui, ces domaines contribuent a creer un climat favorable au dialogue politique et a la cooperation en matiere de securite. S'adressant aux representants etrangers presents a la ceremonie, Vladimir Poutine les a remercies pour leur engagement dans le developpement des relations entre la Russie et leurs pays respectifs. Il a mis en avant l'importance de ces liens, qui constituent, selon lui, une base pour approfondir les echanges et favoriser la comprehension entre les etats. « La cooperation dans les domaines de la culture, de l'education, des relations humanitaires et des affaires cree des conditions favorables au developpement des relations politiques et a la cooperation en matiere de securite », a-t-il explique.

items.title: Théâtre : le Sénégal décroche deux distinctions au FIESAD 2026
items.description: La création théâtrale sénégalaise s’est illustrée au Maroc. À l’occasion de la 12e édition du Festival international des écoles supérieures en art dramatique (FIESAD), organisée du 30 octobre au 2 novembre 2026 à Rabat, le Sénégal a remporté deux distinctions : le prix de la meilleure interprétation masculine et le prix du jury, grâce à la pièce « La Graine de la discorde ». Le Sénégal s'est distingué parmi les pays participants à cette rencontre internationale consacrée à la jeune création théâtrale. Cette édition a réuni des établissements artistiques de sept pays : le Sénégal, Cuba, l’Italie, le Mexique, le Maroc, la Pologne et les Pays-Bas. Une dizaine de représentations ont été proposées au public durant les quatre jours du festival. Présentée par la délégation sénégalaise, « La Graine de la discorde » met en scène une histoire de voisinage qui, à partir d'un différend dérisoire, prend les proportions d'une tragédie collective. L'intrigue commence dans un village où deux hommes, Demba et Mamadou, voient leurs relations se détériorer à cause d'une poule rousse appartenant à Mamadou. L'animal s'introduit dans le champ de Demba et picore quelques graines d'arachide. Furieux, ce dernier décide de tuer la poule de son voisin. Blessé par cet acte, Mamadou choisit à son tour la vengeance. Il met le feu aux champs de Demba, provoquant un incendie qui finit par embraser le village. D'une simple querelle de voisinage naît alors un affrontement qui prend progressivement les dimensions d'une guerre mondiale. À travers cette histoire, la pièce porte une réflexion sur les mécanismes de l'escalade de la violence, l'orgueil et les conséquences parfois démesurées de la vengeance. Elle rappelle notamment qu'un conflit, même né d'un incident insignifiant, peut entraîner des conséquences désastreuses lorsqu'il échappe à toute volonté de dialogue et de réconciliation. La morale de l'œuvre tient en une formule : « Il n'y a pas de querelles, il n'y a que des petits esprits qui ignorent où mène la vengeance. » Avec ces deux distinctions remportées à Rabat, la délégation sénégalaise confirme le potentiel de la jeune création théâtrale nationale et sa capacité à porter, sur les scènes internationales, des récits aux résonances universelles.

items.title: Army kills three suspected kidnappers in Kogi shootout
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the 12 Composite Brigade of the Nigerian Army have killed three suspected kidnappers during a gun battle in Igalamela/Odolu Local Government Area of Kogi State. The troops, operating alongside personnel of the Kogi State Vigilance Service (KSVS), also recovered four AK-47 rifles and a cache of ammunition during a follow-up operation. The Brigade’s spokesman, Lieutenant Hassan Abdullahi, disclosed this in a statement, saying the operation was conducted on November 4, 2026, as part of efforts to dismantle kidnapping networks operating in the area. He said the operation followed earlier raids and exploitation activities in Edimogbo Forest, where suspected kidnappers were believed to be operating. According to him, the joint security team extended its search from Edimogbo Forest towards Obele Forest in pursuit of fleeing suspects. “During the operation, troops made contact with the suspected kidnappers, who attempted to escape upon sighting the security forces. “The encounter resulted in the neutralisation of three suspected kidnappers, while subsequent exploitation of the area led to the recovery of four AK-47 rifles, 12 magazines, 336 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three bandoliers and an identity card,” he said. Abdullahi said the operation was part of sustained efforts to deny criminal elements freedom of movement and dismantle their hideouts through offensive operations and intelligence-driven patrols. He added that maintaining security dominance in the area would help restore confidence among residents of affected communities. The Commander of the 12 Composite Brigade, Brigadier General Kasim Umar Sidi, commended the troops and personnel of the Kogi State Vigilance Service for their resilience and professionalism. He urged them to sustain the momentum and remain vigilant to prevent criminal elements from establishing safe havens within the brigade’s area of responsibility. The Nigerian Army reaffirmed its commitment to protecting lives and property in Kogi State and neighbouring areas, urging residents to provide credible and timely information to security agencies to support ongoing operations. items.title: 2027: Makinde proposes minimum 51% threshold for presidential victory
items.description: …rules out personal benefit from proposed constitutional changes, backs transitional government By Soni Daniel & Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, on Wednesday proposed a minimum 50 per cent-plus-one vote threshold for presidential elections, saying Nigeria needs a political system that compels presidential candidates to secure broader national support before assuming office. Makinde, who unveiled the Reset Nigeria Manifesto in Abuja, also declared that he would not personally benefit from any constitutional and political arrangements that might emerge from his proposed transitional government, insisting that the process must not be manipulated to serve the interests of its promoters. He said the proposed electoral threshold would encourage political parties to build alliances across ethnic, religious and regional divisions, while a transitional government would provide a platform for Nigerians to negotiate a new political and constitutional direction. Offering himself as a test of his commitment to the proposed reforms, Makinde said: “Today, Wednesday, November 4, 2026, I offer myself as a guinea pig by announcing to Nigerians that whatever constitutional and political arrangements we eventually develop, I will not be a beneficiary. “If I intend to benefit personally from the arrangements, there is a possibility that manipulation could set in. But I do not want that to happen.” Explaining the proposed presidential election threshold, the governor argued that candidates should secure sufficient national support to command the respect of the majority rather than emerge through an electoral arrangement that leaves most voters behind. “What we are proposing is that, to become President of Nigeria, a candidate must secure at least 50 per cent plus one vote,” Makinde said. “That way, candidates and political parties will have to engage in discussions across party lines and other divisions to secure the support needed to form a government that commands the respect of the majority of Nigerians.” He identified four fundamental concerns behind his Reset Agenda: the prioritisation of macroeconomic reforms over broad-based economic growth; failure by governments to accept responsibility for results; weak institutions undermined by divisions and bribery; and the exclusion of millions of poor Nigerians from government decisions. Makinde criticised the emphasis on macroeconomic reforms without corresponding improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians, insisting that economic stability must translate into affordable food, employment, improved incomes and a lower cost of living. “My simple proposition is that government must make life easier for the people. That is all,” he said. Questioning the value of economic stability that does not improve household welfare, he added: “What does macroeconomic stability mean if it does not improve the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians?” The governor identified high energy costs as one of the structural problems undermining Nigerian businesses, particularly manufacturers dependent on diesel-powered generators. “For instance, no matter how hard I try, a manufacturer who relies on generators powered by diesel will continue to incur high production costs. We must make it possible for manufacturers to connect to the national electricity grid and access electricity at a lower cost,” he said. He also questioned how the country was managing increased crude oil revenues, arguing that rising international oil prices should produce measurable benefits for Nigerians rather than simply increase government allocations. Makinde, who said he had spent much of his working life in the oil and gas industry, recalled his personal journey from Ibadan to Port-Harcourt in search of opportunities in 1990. “I left Ibadan in early October 1990 with just a bag containing a few belongings, perhaps two pairs of trousers, three or four shirts and a book. The only thing I had was the fare to travel to Kaduna with my degree,” he recalled. He said he eventually secured employment, established a business, raised a family and built his life, experiences that informed his conviction that government policies must create opportunities for ordinary Nigerians. On accountability, Makinde promised that his proposed administration would establish measurable performance targets within its first 100 days and make its achievements subject to public scrutiny. Electricity & Petroleum Pricing He also faulted the Federal Government’s handling of the electricity sector, arguing that the transfer of regulatory powers to states should not become an excuse for abandoning national responsibilities. “Yes, but should a baby that has just been born start crawling, walking and running at the same time?” he asked. He maintained that while states should develop their electricity markets according to their capacities, the Federal Government must continue to manage national electricity assets and address challenges affecting generation and distribution. Makinde further called for continuity in national development policies irrespective of changes in political parties, citing the succession of different administrations in Oyo State since 1999. “Political parties will come and go, but our national development plans and the things we must do for our people must remain constant. We must continue to implement them, irrespective of the political party in power,” he said. On petroleum pricing, he questioned the argument that lower fuel prices in Nigeria would encourage smuggling into neighbouring countries, insisting that the government should strengthen border management rather than transfer the consequences of enforcement failures to citizens. He also advocated a new social and political order in which institutions would function across party and regional differences, adding that more than half of Nigeria’s population lived in poverty and should not be treated as an afterthought in government decisions. Makinde said the Reset Agenda was developed through extensive consultations and town hall meetings across the six geopolitical zones, where Nigerians were asked to articulate their expectations of government. He recalled that some participants had challenged him to provide the kind of leadership associated with Nigeria’s founding fathers, including Tafawa Balewa, Obafemi Awolowo and Nnamdi Azikiwe. Opposition complementary to govt, says Daura Earlier, the APM vice-presidential candidate, Lawal Daura, called for a national conference involving government representatives and all segments of Nigerian society to resolve the country’s longstanding political contradictions. Daura, who described the first government under their proposed arrangement as transitional, said the process would allow Nigerians to discuss their differences, reach agreements and establish a common direction for the country. He warned against attempts by governments to weaken opposition parties, arguing that effective opposition was necessary for political stability and democratic development. “The opposition is complementary to the government; it is not an enemy of the government,” he said. Daura maintained that the suppression of political opponents and denial of a level playing field ultimately threatened the country and its citizens. He said opposition parties should be allowed to participate freely in the political process, adding that the quality of opposition could help reduce political tension and strengthen democratic institutions. Don’t use state institutions to undermine democracy, Dantalle warns Also speaking, National Chairman of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM, Yusuf Dantalle, warned against attempts to use state institutions to undermine democratic competition, urging political leaders to protect the country’s democratic institutions. Dantalle questioned the gap between the promises made by the governing All Progressives Congress, APC, during its election campaigns and the economic realities Nigerians were currently facing. He criticised rising petroleum prices and the burden of taxation on citizens and businesses, arguing that the country’s economic difficulties required urgent attention. The APM chairman also urged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to discharge its responsibilities impartially and ensure that electoral activities were conducted in an atmosphere of peace. He warned that electoral fraud amounted to a denial of citizens’ democratic rights because it deprived them of the opportunity to choose their leaders. Dantalle said the younger generation was looking up to political leaders to protect the country’s democratic future and called for collective efforts to prevent the weakening of democratic institutions. In his remarks, National Chairman of the Social Democratic Party, SDP, Prof. Sadiq Gombe, described Makinde as a leading figure in the opposition, recalling how he won the 2019 Oyo governorship election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, despite the dominance of the APC in the South-West at the time. Gombe also praised Makinde and Bauchi State Governor, Bala Mohammed, for sustaining opposition cooperation, saying their efforts had helped rekindle democratic engagement among political parties. He recalled that when the SDP struggled to secure a venue for its convention in Abuja, it eventually approached Mohammed, who offered Bauchi State as an alternative venue. Gombe said Makinde also hosted an initiative that brought opposition political parties together, adding that the engagement had encouraged further consultations among political leaders and presidential aspirants. He urged opposition leaders to embrace humility, patriotism and cooperation in their efforts to strengthen democracy. items.title: Beyond oil and gold: Ghana and Saudi Arabia build a new era of economic cooperation
items.description: The future of investment is no longer shaped by capital alone. It is increasingly shaped by strategic partnerships, policy credibility, and countries’ ability to connect opportunity with confidence. Ghana’s engagement with Saudi Arabia’s investment community in Riyadh reflects a deliberate economic diplomacy strategy to translate national development priorities into international investment partnerships. An investment webinar organised by the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), in collaboration with the Embassy of Ghana in Riyadh, provided a platform to present Ghana’s economic opportunities, investment reforms and development priorities to prospective investors in the Kingdom. Held under the theme, “Ghana is Open for Business: Unlocking Opportunities for Investors,” the engagement formed part of GIPA’s broader mandate to promote Ghana as a competitive investment destination and facilitate partnerships that support economic transformation. The initiative is aligned with the strategic direction of GIPA’s Chief Executive Officer, Simon Madjie, whose leadership has emphasised stronger international investor engagement, closer collaboration with Ghana’s diplomatic missions and the attraction of investments that create jobs, strengthen industries and accelerate value creation. Investment p romotion as an e conomic s trategy In the modern global economy, investment promotion has moved beyond the attraction of financial resources. Countries increasingly seek investments that contribute to productivity, technology transfer, export competitiveness and sustainable development. Ghana’s approach reflects this broader understanding. Through the Regional and Global Operations Division (RGOD), GIPA is leveraging Ghana’s diplomatic network as a bridge between international investors and opportunities within the Ghanaian economy. At the Riyadh engagement, Victoria Cobbah, Head of the RGOD, highlighted Ghana’s democratic stability, predictable regulatory environment and investor protection framework as key factors supporting business confidence. She also drew attention to Ghana’s strategic position as host of the Secretariat of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), providing investors with access to a continental market of more than 1.4 billion people. For Saudi investors, this presents an opportunity to use Ghana not only as a destination market, but also as a base for accessing wider African markets. Aligning Ghana’s p riorities with Saudi v ision 2030 The engagement also revealed significant areas of policy alignment between Ghana’s development agenda and Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030. Both countries are pursuing economic diversification, private-sector growth, infrastructure expansion, renewable energy development and technological advancement. This alignment creates opportunities for partnerships in agriculture, manufacturing, logistics, energy, healthcare, tourism and digital services. Ghana’s investment proposition is increasingly centred on sectors capable of generating economic value beyond traditional commodity exports. Government i nterventions s upporting g rowth Ghana’s investment drive is reinforced by government initiatives designed to address structural challenges and create a stronger environment for private enterprise. The Big Push Programme represents government’s commitment to expanding infrastructure, particularly roads, transport networks and productive assets needed to improve business efficiency. In agriculture, the Agriculture for Economic Transformation Agenda seeks to reposition the sector through commercialisation, mechanisation, irrigation and agro-processing. The objective is to create stronger agricultural value chains in which investors can participate in production, processing, storage and export. The Digital Jobs Initiative reflects Ghana’s commitment to preparing its young population for the digital economy by expanding technology skills and supporting innovation-driven employment. Meanwhile, initiatives such as the Black Star Experience and the Marine Drive Project demonstrate efforts to unlock investment opportunities in tourism, culture, hospitality and real estate. Building i nvestor c onfidence t hrough d ialogue The interactive session provided Saudi businesses with an opportunity to explore practical issues affecting investment decisions. Yusif Mustapha of the Regional and Global Operations Division addressed concerns relating to foreign ownership, investment protection and business establishment in Ghana. He explained that foreign investors can establish businesses in Ghana under applicable laws, including arrangements that permit full foreign ownership. He further highlighted the ability of investors to repatriate profits and dividends, reinforcing Ghana’s commitment to investor protection. Participants also expressed interest in improved aviation connectivity between Ghana and Saudi Arabia, as well as developments in transport infrastructure. Discussions on projects such as the Volta Economic Corridor highlighted Ghana’s ambition to strengthen regional connectivity and improve trade facilitation. Diplomacy s upporting i nvestment The participation of Alhaji Said Sinare, Ambassador of Ghana to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, demonstrated the growing importance of economic diplomacy in strengthening commercial relations. The Ambassador encouraged Saudi investors to explore opportunities in Ghana’s minerals, agriculture, energy and manufacturing sectors, while reaffirming the Embassy’s readiness to support investors. The Riyadh engagement ultimately reinforced a central message: Ghana’s investment strategy is not simply about attracting capital; it is about building partnerships that support shared economic progress. Ghana Investment Promotion Authority e quips g lobal m issions to c hampion e conomic g rowth In a world where countries compete not only for markets but also for investment, diplomacy is taking on a new economic role. Foreign missions are increasingly becoming bridges between national ambitions and global investors seeking stable, credible and high-growth destinations. Ghana is embracing this shift by empowering its diplomatic missions with the knowledge and tools needed to promote the country’s investment opportunities more effectively. As part of this strategy, GIPA, under the leadership of Chief Executive Officer Simon Madjie, is strengthening collaboration with Ghana’s missions abroad to position the country as a preferred destination for sustainable investment. This vision was demonstrated through a capacity-building webinar organised for officials of the Ghana Mission in Brussels, aimed at enhancing their understanding of Ghana’s economic landscape, government priorities and emerging investment opportunities. Connecting p olicy with i nvestment o pportunities The session was led by Ms Victoria Cobbah, Head of the Regional and Global Operations Division (RGOD) at GIPA, who provided insights into Ghana’s economic agenda, investment initiatives, competitive advantages and incentives available to investors. The engagement highlighted government’s commitment to building a resilient and competitive economy anchored on macroeconomic stability, industrial growth, productivity and private-sector participation. Key policy initiatives presented included the Big Push Agenda, which seeks to accelerate infrastructure development and improve economic connectivity; the 24-Hour Economy Programme, designed to increase productivity and create new employment opportunities; and the Volta Economic Corridor Project, which aims to unlock economic potential through improved transport, agriculture and industrial development. Other strategic programmes highlighted included the Goldbod initiative, the Agro-Ecological Parks Programme, the Sahel Cargo Hub Strategy and the Import Substitution Industrialisation Programme. Together, these initiatives demonstrate Ghana’s ambition to move beyond raw commodity exports towards a value-driven economy in which investors can participate in manufacturing, processing, innovation and job creation. Ghana’s i nvestment a dvantage Ghana’s investment proposition is built on stability, opportunity and access. The webinar highlighted the country’s democratic credentials, peaceful business environment, strategic location and growing consumer market as key factors supporting investor confidence. Ghana’s role as host of the AfCFTA Secretariat was also emphasised as a major advantage, providing investors with a gateway to Africa’s expanding single market. The country’s improving infrastructure, growing digital economy and investment incentives, including Free Zones benefits and sector-specific incentives, further strengthen Ghana’s competitiveness. Brussels m ission e xplores s trategic s ectors For Ambassador Henry Tachie-Menson, Ghana’s Ambassador to Belgium, the engagement provided an opportunity to deepen the Mission’s understanding of priority sectors and strengthen its ability to engage potential investors. The discussions focused on areas with strong investment potential, including renewable energy, critical minerals, cocoa, agriculture, technology, real estate, mining infrastructure and AfCFTA-related opportunities. In energy, attention was drawn to opportunities in solar power, hydrogen development, lithium processing and sustainable energy solutions. The cocoa sector emerged as another important area, with opportunities identified in cocoa butter, liquor, powder and chocolate manufacturing. The need to promote research and innovation through institutions such as the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana and the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research was also highlighted. Creating v alue a cross g rowth s ectors Agriculture remains a major investment opportunity, with prospects in poultry, animal-feed production, livestock farming, irrigation, greenhouse farming and modern agricultural technologies. Technology and digital services were also identified as emerging areas for investors as Ghana continues to expand its digital economy. In real estate, opportunities exist in affordable housing, commercial developments and student accommodation, supported by Ghana’s growing housing demand and incentives for qualifying affordable housing projects. Strengthening i nvestor c onfidence t hrough p artnership The webinar also created space for dialogue on investor concerns, including taxation, incentives, infrastructure costs and gold traceability. GIPA provided updates on measures to strengthen transparency in the minerals sector through Goldbod, while highlighting opportunities in lithium value addition, cocoa processing, renewable energy and industrial development. The engagement concluded with commitments to deepen collaboration between GIPA and the Ghana Mission in Brussels through investment materials, sector information sharing and joint promotional activities. Ambassador Tachie-Menson reaffirmed the Mission’s commitment to the “Investing in Ghana” agenda and encouraged further collaboration, including participation in upcoming investment events in Belgium. Through initiatives such as these, Ghana is demonstrating that economic diplomacy is no longer only about representation. It is about creating partnerships, attracting investment and building a stronger future through shared growth.

items.title: Tinubu returns 1m out-of-school children to classrooms – APC PCC
items.description: …Says NELFUND disbursed ₦372.62bn in student loans By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has disclosed that President Bola Tinubu’s administration has returned over one million out-of-school children to classrooms. The Council said this in a statement on Wednesday by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, citing the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) 2026 report of the Federal Ministry of Education. The report credits the Better Education Service Delivery for All (BESDA) programme for the feat. It also says the programme trained 1,400 Tsangaya teachers and set up 200 bilingual centres across 17 northern states. The Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE) has reached 7.19 million girls, of whom 3.7 million are enrolled in secondary schools. Over 10,000 schools have also benefited from improved facilities, according to the council. On funding, the Federal Government reportedly allocated a record ₦3.52 trillion to education in the 2026 budget. It also secured $552 million for a basic education programme targeting 29 million children, over 500,000 teachers and 65,000 public schools. According to the council, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund NELFUND has processed 1,659,853 student loan applications and disbursed ₦372.62 billion. Of this, ₦192.89 billion went to tuition and ₦179.73 billion to upkeep allowances, across 319 tertiary institutions. The statement said the administration has resolved the age-long dispute with the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and implemented the agreement providing for a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and improved welfare benefits. The Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund, it added, has paid out ₦28 billion to 15,000 workers in 153 public institutions. Eligible staff can access loans of up to ₦10 million for housing, healthcare, transportation and education. On technical and vocational education and training (TVET), the scheme has drawn over 2.8 million applications. A total of 156,446 verified trainees are receiving free training, monthly stipends and start-up support. Alake said more than ₦65.7 billion has been disbursed to trainees and ₦30.2 billion to training centres. Thirty-eight technical colleges have been rehabilitated, and technical education now covers tuition, boarding, textbooks and uniforms at no cost to students. On teacher development, Alake said 53,553 teachers have registered under EduRevamp, and 51,794 have joined the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway (ATPP). The six-month programme offers professional qualifications, certification and licensing. Backed by ₦2 billion, it targets 250,000 teachers by 2027, he added. Alake added that in medical education, ₦110 billion is going into rehabilitating 18 federal medical schools across the six geopolitical zones. Nursing enrolment rose from 81,480 in 2023 to 114,300 in 2025. Twenty science, technology, engineering and medical sciences institutions have been approved, and 12 engineering and technology faculties are targeted for rehabilitation. The Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, said the success of the reforms would be judged by their impact on students, teachers and institutions, not by the money allocated or the number of programmes introduced. “Our measure of success is not merely the amount of money allocated to education or the number of programmes introduced. It is the difference these interventions make in the lives of our children, students, teachers and institutions,” he said.
