items.title: «L’unité des peuples constitue le socle de la souveraineté et de l’indépendance de la Russie», affirme Poutine lors de la Journée de l’unité nationale
items.description: Vladimir Poutine a participe, le 4 novembre a Moscou, a la seance pleniere de la Semaine des peuples de Russie. Le president russe y a souligne le role essentiel de l'unite nationale dans la preservation de la souverainete et de l'independance du pays. « L'entente, le respect mutuel et l'unite des peuples de Russie constituent le socle de la souverainete et de l'independance de notre pays », a-t-il declare. Organisee a l'occasion de la Journee de l'unite nationale, cette rencontre a egalement ete marquee par un rappel historique. Vladimir Poutine a evoque la liberation de Moscou en 1612 par la milice populaire de Kouzma Minine et Dmitri Pojarski, composee de personnes de differentes nationalites. Selon lui, cet episode illustre le role determinant de la solidarite entre les peuples dans l'histoire russe. Le chef de l'etat a egalement appele a preserver cette cohesion en prevenant toute tentative d'attiser les tensions entre les communautes et de fragiliser la stabilite sociale. La diversite culturelle et la place centrale de la langue russe Vladimir Poutine a salue la diversite des peuples, des cultures et des traditions, qu'il considere comme l'une des grandes forces de la Russie. Il a rappele que leurs cultures s'etaient profondement melees au fil des siecles, formant un patrimoine commun tout en conservant leurs particularites. Le president a reaffirme que le peuple russe et la langue russe demeuraient le fondement de l'etat. Il a insiste sur leur role federateur dans la preservation des cultures et des identites des autres peuples de la Federation, soulignant que le soutien a la langue et a la culture russes revetait une importance strategique. La Semaine des peuples de Russie, organisee du 2 au 9 novembre, s'inscrit dans cette demarche. Elle vise a mettre en valeur le patrimoine de plus de 190 peuples et a developper les echanges culturels internationaux. Vladimir Poutine a notamment salue les initiatives associant traditions et economie creative, comme l'exposition « Âme de la Russie ». Il a egalement souligne que des representants de plus de cent peuples de la Federation avaient recu de hautes distinctions d'etat pour leur courage et leur heroïsme lors de l'operation militaire speciale. Au Kremlin, la solidarite nationale mise a l'honneur Vladimir Poutine a ensuite participe au Kremlin a une ceremonie de remise de distinctions d'etat et de prix recompensant les contributions au renforcement de l'unite nationale. Le president a salue le soutien sincere et concret apporte par la population aux militaires engages dans l'operation militaire speciale. Il a rappele que les citoyens de differentes ethnicites, cultures et religions partageaient une meme patrie, tout en restant attaches a leurs origines. evoquant les grandes epreuves de l'histoire russe, il a affirme que la cohesion de la population et la volonte de decider librement de l'avenir du pays avaient toujours permis a la Russie de relever les defis auxquels elle etait confrontee. Parmi les personnalites distinguees, Ivan Essine, directeur du Fonds des projets humanitaires, a recu le prix presidentiel pour sa contribution a l'unite nationale. Son organisation developpe le reseau de parcs historiques « La Russie, mon histoire », qui compte 26 sites et a accueilli plus de 30 millions de visiteurs, expositions temporaires comprises. Le chef de l'etat a enfin salue les personnalites etrangeres œuvrant au renforcement des liens humanitaires avec la Russie, mettant en avant la portee internationale de sa culture et de ses traditions. « La culture, les traditions et les valeurs russes unissent de nombreuses personnes dans le monde », a-t-il declare.

Minority invokes Danquah-Dombo-Busia tradition in pledge to defend democracy
items.description: The Minority in Parliament has invoked the Danquah-Dombo-Busia political tradition, pledging to continue defending democracy, freedom and the rights of Ghanaians. Speaking at a press conference outside the Chamber on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin said the tradition was rooted in the United Party and reflected Ghana’s diverse ethnic, religious and regional heritage. The press conference follows the ejection of Damongo MP Samuel Abu Jinapor from the parliamentary Chamber after he alleged that diplomatic passports were being sold for between $10,000 and $50,000. The Minority staged a solidarity walkout in response to his removal, with its subsequent public statements focusing on parliamentary accountability, democratic freedoms and what the caucus describes as intimidation of opposition lawmakers. He said the caucus considered itself part of a political inheritance built on the efforts of generations who had worked to protect and consolidate the country’s democracy. “Ours is the Danquah-Dombo-Busia tradition rooted in the United Party and the inheritance of Ghanaian tribes, kingdoms, religions and regions, and generations united to protect, restore and consolidate our democracy,” he stated. Mr Afenyo-Markin said the Minority would not be intimidated or deterred from holding the government accountable. “We owe them fidelity. We owe our children every Ghanaian freedom. Cowardice is not in our DNA. Fear is a stranger to our heartbeat. Intimidation cannot break our spirits. Bullies cannot extinguish our fire to stand and fight for what is right without fright,” he said. He added that the caucus would continue to hold the government and its officials accountable, saying that was the responsibility entrusted to them by Ghanaians. “We shall hold the government and its functionaries accountable as Ghanaians have entrusted us to do,” he stated. The Minority Leader described the caucus as small in numbers but resolute in its commitment to its political principles. “We are few, but firm in conviction. This is who we are. May God protect us in the service of our people. And may God bless our homeland Ghana and make our nation great and strong, bold to defend forever the cause of freedom and of rights,” he said. He thanked journalists and concluded the press conference.

items.title: Cybersecurity incidents resulted in over GH₵209m in losses between January and September – CSA
items.description: Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority (CSA), Dr Divine Selasi Agbeti, has said a total of 4,938 cybersecurity incidents were recorded in the country between January and September this year, resulting in financial losses exceeding GH¢209.7 million, He said the figure represented more than ninefold increase in financial losses compared to the GH¢22.5 million recorded from 4,604 incidents last year. He said human error and social engineering accounted for between 60 and 95 per cent of cybersecurity incidents, making public awareness and responsible digital behaviour essential in preventing online crimes. Dr Agbesi said this during the Northern Regional Cybersecurity Awareness campaign, organised by the CSA in Tamale on Tuesday. The day’s event was attended by representatives of public institutions, NGOs, students, and members of the public, among others. It formed part of activities marking this year’s National Cybersecurity Awareness Month, an annual initiative aimed at raising awareness about emerging cyber threats, promoting responsible digital behaviour and equipping individuals and institutions with the knowledge to protect themselves against cybercrime. It also seeks to encourage collective responsibility in securing the country’s digital environment, especially as more people rely on mobile money, internet banking, and other digital financial services. Dr Agbesi said the development highlighted the growing threat of cybercrime and the need for individuals, businesses and public institutions to strengthen their cybersecurity measures. He cautioned users of mobile money, internet banking, and digital wallets against fraudulent investment schemes, impersonation, and attempts by criminals to obtain their sensitive personal information. He said cybersecurity was a shared responsibility and urged individuals to protect their digital accounts, institutions to prioritise cybersecurity investments and the public to share online safety information with family members and communities. He encouraged members of the public to report suspected cybercrime incidents to the CSA through its 24-hour short code 292, and seek guidance before undertaking online transactions they were uncertain about. He announced that the CSA would establish a zonal office in Tamale to strengthen cybersecurity awareness, incident reporting and response across the northern sector of the country. He said the office would bring the CSA’s services closer to communities and improve collaboration with stakeholders in addressing cyber threats. The Northern Regional Minister, Ali Adolf John, whose speech was read on his behalf, mentioned online investment fraud, mobile money scams and fake employment offers as some of the common cybercrime threats in the region. He said job seekers and individuals seeking to improve their financial circumstances were especially vulnerable to fraudulent schemes promising employment opportunities and financial returns in exchange for upfront payments. He expressed concern about deceptive recruitment and travel arrangements allegedly linked to criminal operations, calling for stronger collaboration amongst the CSA, the Ghana Police Service and other security agencies to address the threats. He lauded plans to establish a CSA zonal office in Tamale and said it would strengthen cybersecurity education, technical support and institutional collaboration. The National Cyber Security Awareness Officer, CSA, Mary Ama Bawa, urged the youth to recognise the opportunities and threats associated with digital platforms and avoid becoming perpetrators or victims of cybercrime. The Dean of the Faculty of Applied Science and Technology, Tamale Technical University (TaTU), Professor Abukari Abdul Aziz Danaa, said the growing reliance on digital financial services had exposed users to increasingly sophisticated fraudulent activities. He cited fraudulent promotional messages, impersonation of mobile money agents, and fake payment screenshots as some of the methods used by cybercriminals to defraud unsuspecting people. He urged users to verify transactions through their accounts and trusted channels before releasing goods or acting on payment notifications. Prof. Danaa urged financial institutions to strengthen their security systems to detect unusual transactions and flag suspicious activities for further verification. He said TaTU had commenced undergraduate and master’s degree programmes in cybersecurity to develop skilled professionals capable of responding to emerging digital threats.

items.title: Susan Collins Didn’t Have a Chance
items.description: T he realization that Susan Collins would lose her bid for a sixth Senate term dawned slowly on the Republicans gathered last night in a hotel ballroom in Bangor, Maine. Democrats were notching victories up and down the Eastern Seaboard, and the wave was quickly spreading to Kansas, Texas, and points west. But Collins had confounded the doomsayers before. Republicans here believed she would undoubtedly do it again. “She’s sure to win,” a conservative activist, Tom Burpee, proclaimed to me shortly after 9 p.m. A few minutes earlier, another Republican had marched through the ballroom with a similarly confident prediction: “Maine,” he told me, “isn’t that stupid.” Collins, too, betrayed no hint of concern. Around 9:40 p.m., she made a long, beaming pass through the party. As Journey’s “Don’t Stop Believin’” filled the room, Collins accepted hugs and handshakes, small gifts and words of encouragement. She peered at the laptop screen of a Republican staffer who showed her a rosy analysis of the latest returns. Maine counts its votes at an agonizing pace, and as Collins worked the crowd, it was still possible for Republicans to believe she might defy the odds one more time. Collins’s stroll around the ballroom was, in retrospect, not a victory lap but a farewell. She would not return to the party. Shortly after midnight, she called the Democrat Troy Jackson to congratulate him on his win. By that late hour, the ballroom throng had thinned to just a few dozen people, and Collins made no concession speech. She was the longest-serving Republican incumbent to lose a reelection bid last night. With almost 90 percent of votes counted this morning, Jackson was up by nearly eight points. “It has been the honor of my life to serve the people of Maine in the United States Senate,” Collins said in a brief statement. Democrats in Maine were only slightly less surprised to have finally ousted the most resilient of Republican senators. As Jackson pulled ahead of Collins in the polls during the closing weeks of the race, many Democrats found their optimism tempered by memories of the last time they tried to defeat her. Heading into Election Day in 2020, Collins was projected to lose to Sara Gideon, a well-funded former legislative leader in Maine. But Collins won, defeating Gideon by nearly the same margin—about nine points—that Joe Biden had when he prevailed over Donald Trump in Maine that year. This year’s campaign was far more tumultuous for Democrats, and Jackson was not the candidate they thought—or hoped—they’d be running against Collins. A former logger who spent most of the past two decades in the state legislature, Jackson had campaigned for governor and finished third in the primary. But after Graham Platner’s Senate candidacy collapsed following allegations of sexual assault (which he denied), Jackson emerged as a potential replacement, and he won a quick-fire nominating convention in July. Jackson, like Platner, is a progressive in the mold of Bernie Sanders . He campaigned on Medicare for All and vowed to oppose another term for Chuck Schumer as the Democratic Senate leader. But Jackson also previously held positions that made his campaign more complicated than the party would have liked. Democrats have assailed Collins for her support for Justices Brett Kavanaugh and Neil Gorsuch, Trump appointees to the Supreme Court who voted to overturn Roe v. Wade . Yet whereas Collins has long claimed to support abortion rights, Jackson was an opponent of legal abortion at the beginning of his career. “Troy evolved. Susan Collins devolved,” Mini Timmaraju, CEO of the abortion-rights advocacy group Reproductive Freedom for All, told reporters as she campaigned for Jackson on Monday. After 30 years, Maine has evolved as well. C ollins reprised the message that won her a fifth term in 2020. She ran as Maine’s guardian in Washington, leaning on her reputation as a moderate who works across the aisle and on her ability to bring home billions of dollars in federal funding as chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee. Both Jackson and Collins grew up in the same rural county in northern Maine, not far from the Canadian border. Despite Jackson’s many years as a leader in Maine’s legislature, Collins treated him as a novice who’d be in over his head in Washington. A Collins ad late in the campaign made the point more explicitly. “We’re not talking about buying a cord of wood here,” the retired Maine broadcaster Bill Green said in the commercial, a reference to Jackson’s logging background. “We’re sending someone to the U.S. Senate, and Troy doesn’t have the tools he needs to be effective.” [ Read: How the Democrats beat Trump ] During their four debates, Jackson usually referred to her as “Senator Collins.” She just called him “Troy,” a choice that suggested small-state friendliness but was really designed to accentuate the stature gap. When Jackson told Collins to “shut up” during the final debate, her campaign linked the remark to reports that, as a legislator, Jackson was bullying and intimidating toward women. Jackson denied that charge—a former colleague at one point told reporters that he sometimes lost his temper, though not “in a gendered way.” But voters in this election were angry, too, and eager to rebuff conventional politicians. Jackson was happy to engage in a debate over who was more senatorial, seeking to turn Collins’s experience into a liability. He dressed as a cord of wood for Halloween and concluded his campaign Monday night at a Portland bowling alley, where he returned to the populist theme of his candidacy. “I’ve waited so long for everyday people to rise up and demand a government that works for them,” Jackson told his cheering supporters. As he made stops around Portland on Monday, Jackson tried to project a sense of optimism. “I’ve got a good feeling about this,” he told a group of volunteers at a canvass launch. He wasn’t entirely convincing. Mostly, Jackson just seemed exhausted, frequently rubbing his eyes and reminding his supporters—and possibly himself—that the campaign was almost over. Monday marked the 100th day of his Senate campaign, a sprint that was faster even than Kamala Harris’s abbreviated presidential campaign in 2024. By the end, Jackson had managed to mostly set aside concerns that he would be unable to marshal the excitement among younger, progressive voters that Platner had initially generated. Al Huntley, a retiree who was hosting a canvass launch in South Portland, told me that he encountered a few diehards who planned to write in Platner’s name, “but not many.” Both Huntley and his wife, Pauline, told me they were feeling confident about Jackson’s chances. But they said they’d felt the same way about Gideon as the election closed six years ago. “So I’m skittish,” Pauline Huntley said. Such was the prevailing mood among Democrats I encountered throughout the final weeks of the campaign—the tentative belief, if not the conviction, that Collins’s hold on Maine voters had loosened, and that voters were angry enough with Trump and Republicans to oust a 30-year incumbent. “I am allowing myself to hope that she will lose,” Jennifer Tingle, a 64-year-old educator, told me at a Jackson rally in Lewiston. Perhaps the Democrats did not have to fret as much as they did. Their national landslide proved far too big for a blue-state Republican to overcome, and a race that both parties once thought might determine control of the Senate instead became just one more in an enormous pile of Democratic triumphs. By this morning, Democrats had a path to controlling up to 56 Senate seats next year. The nationwide rout offered a measure of solace for Collins’s supporters. “It’s not a vote against her,” one of them told me. David Whitney, a local GOP chair, suggested that there was little more Collins could have done. “In 2024, Republicans spoke loud and clear,” Whitney told me; “2026 is the Democrats’ turn to do the same.” A Collins loss, after a long run of dominance, had been difficult for many in Maine to fathom. But to some Republicans in Bangor, as the full picture of the GOP’s midterm wipeout became clear last night, it came instead to seem inevitable.

items.title: Lutte contre la fraude : Plus de 95 millions F CFA de marchandises saisies en deux semaines par la CNLF
items.description: Du gasoil vendu en violation de la réglementation au cyanure dissimulé dans une cargaison de clinker, en passant par les sachets plastiques interdits et le riz importé frauduleusement, les services de la Coordination Nationale de Lutte Contre la Fraude (CNLF) multiplient les opérations de contrôle sur le territoire national. Entre le 17 et le 30 octobre 2026, leurs interventions ont permis de saisir des marchandises d'une valeur estimée à plus de 95 millions de F CFA. Un bilan présenté le mardi 3 novembre 2026 à Diébougou. Sur les routes, dans les magasins de stockage et aux différents points de contrôle, la lutte contre la fraude prend plusieurs formes. Derrière les marchandises qui circulent se cachent parfois des pratiques commerciales illicites, des produits interdits ou des importations qui échappent aux règles établies. C'est contre ces pratiques que les équipes de la Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la fraude (CNLF) sont mobilisées. Entre le 17 et le 30 octobre 2026, cette mission de contrôle a donné lieu à plusieurs interventions dans différentes localités du Burkina Faso. À Ouagadougou, les premières opérations remontent au 17 octobre. Ce jour-là, les agents interceptent une citerne transportant 14 000 litres de gasoil. En cause, une pratique illicite de prix. Cette saisie illustre la vigilance des services de contrôle face aux irrégularités qui affectent le marché des hydrocarbures. Trois jours plus tard, le 20 octobre, une autre découverte vient illustrer la diversité des produits concernés par ce combat. Dans une cargaison de clinker, les agents mettent au jour 20 sacs de cyanure de 50 kg chacun. Au total, une tonne de cette substance est ainsi interceptée. Dissimulé dans un chargement de matériaux, ce produit chimique constitue un enjeu particulier de contrôle, au regard des risques que peuvent représenter les substances dangereuses lorsqu'elles échappent aux circuits réglementaires. De l'axe Dakola à Bobo-Dioulasso, la vigilance se poursuit Le 28 octobre, toujours à Ouagadougou, les équipes poursuivent leurs investigations. Dans un magasin, elles découvrent des sachets plastiques interdits ainsi que de l'huile de lubrification contrefaite. Une intervention qui rappelle que la lutte contre la fraude ne concerne pas uniquement les marchandises circulant sur les grands axes routiers. Elle s'étend également aux espaces de stockage et aux circuits de distribution. La surveillance ne se limite pas à la capitale. Sur l'axe Dakola, les services de la CNLF interceptent des boissons de marque ICE dont l'importation est interdite. Cette opération traduit l'importance des contrôles sur les voies de circulation des marchandises, notamment pour empêcher l'introduction de produits soumis à des restrictions. À Bobo-Dioulasso, la Brigade d'enquête et de recherche de l'Ouest réalise une autre saisie d'envergure. Elle met la main sur un stock de 55 tonnes de riz importé en dépit des mesures d'interdiction d'importation de cette denrée. Par cette intervention, les agents s'attaquent à une pratique susceptible de fragiliser les mesures nationales de régulation du marché et de protection de la production locale. Du carburant au riz, en passant par les produits chimiques et les emballages plastiques, ces différentes opérations révèlent l'étendue du front sur lequel les services de contrôle sont engagés. Chaque saisie répond à une problématique particulière qu’est le respect des règles de fixation des prix, le contrôle des substances dangereuses, la protection de l'environnement et l’application des mesures encadrant les importations. La lutte contre la fraude vise à préserver la sécurité et la santé des consommateurs Au terme de cette séquence d'opérations, le bilan financier dépasse les 95 millions de F CFA. Pour le coordonnateur national de lutte contre la fraude, le Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, ces résultats sont le fruit de l'engagement et de la vigilance des agents déployés sur le terrain. « Nous tenons à les féliciter pour leur professionnalisme et pour leur savoir-faire, pour leur vigilance accrue en matière de lutte contre la fraude », a-t-il déclaré, saluant le travail accompli par les différentes équipes. Mais derrière les chiffres et les quantités saisies, le responsable met surtout en avant un enjeu de protection des populations. La lutte contre la fraude vise, selon lui, à préserver la sécurité et la santé des consommateurs, en empêchant notamment la circulation de produits dont l'importation, la commercialisation ou l'utilisation ne respectent pas les dispositions en vigueur. Le combat comporte également une dimension économique. En veillant à l'application de la réglementation commerciale, la CNLF entend contribuer à assainir les circuits d'approvisionnement et à préserver les intérêts de l'économie nationale. Pour le Dr Mohamadi Compaoré, la lutte contre la fraude ne saurait reposer uniquement sur les agents de contrôle. Elle nécessite aussi l'adhésion des commerçants, des importateurs et de l'ensemble des acteurs économiques. Il les invite ainsi à accompagner les orientations des autorités burkinabè dans le contexte de la Révolution progressiste populaire. « Nous allons toujours accentuer la vigilance pour les amener de force à abandonner ces pratiques frauduleuses », Dr Mohamadi Compaoré « Nous sommes dans une phase de Révolution Progressiste Populaire. Tout le monde doit s'aligner, tout le monde doit accompagner le gouvernement pour que nous puissions sortir notre pays du sous-développement », a-t-il insisté. Le coordonnateur national prévient que les contrôles vont se poursuivre et s'intensifier. Face aux acteurs qui persistent dans les pratiques frauduleuses, la CNLF entend maintenir la pression. « Nous allons toujours accentuer la vigilance pour les amener de force à abandonner ces pratiques frauduleuses », a-t-il averti. Des axes routiers aux lieux de stockage, en passant par les circuits d'importation, le combat se joue sur plusieurs fronts. Avec ces marchandises interceptées en quatorze jours, la CNLF affiche sa détermination à faire respecter la réglementation et à défendre les intérêts des consommateurs et de l'économie burkinabè. Basile SAMA Faso7 L’article Lutte contre la fraude : Plus de 95 millions F CFA de marchandises saisies en deux semaines par la CNLF est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: ECP objects to retired SC judge's remarks about 2023 ruling on polls in Punjab and KP, reserved seats case
items.description: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday objected to remarks made by former senior puisne judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, Mansoor Ali Shah, regarding polls in KP and Punjab and the reserved seats case pertaining to the PTI. Shah made the remarks at an event organised by the US-based Community Alliance for Peace and Justice on October 29, where he was asked about his dissenting opinion in the 2023 SC ruling on provincial elections in Punjab and KP and whether it was a “turning point” and the beginning of a “division” within the SC. In its 3-2 verdict, the SC, after taking a suo motu notice, directed that elections should be held within 90 days in both provinces. Two judges, including Shah, had dissented from the ruling, saying that the suo motu proceedings initiated by then-chief justice of Pakistan Umar Ata Bandial, were “wholly unjustified”, besides being initiated with “undue haste”. In their detailed reasoning , they explained that the SC by a majority of 4-3 and not 3-2 had dismissed the suo motu hearing on polls delay in Punjab and KP and therefore the same should be considered as the “Order of the Court”. It had resulted in a controversy, with the government igniting a raging debate claiming that the ruling was a 4-3 majority decision in its favour and not a 3-2 verdict against. In response to the question, Shah said that this was the time when the ex-chief justice was forming “like-minded benches”, adding that three or four judges were attending to the majority of the cases. He said that initially the matter was taken by the high courts. He said that the SC judges had gathered in the ante-room and discussed with the chief justice at the time that suo motu notice should not be taken at this point. He said that it was “agreed” to wait but days later a SC bench took up the matter under suo motu powers as he denounced the “one-man show” going on at the time. He said that at the time, two SC judges — Justice Yahya Afridi and Justice Athar Minallah — had dismissed the petitions in the case. He said that the SC bench was later reconstituted, adding that since two judges had decided the matter, the verdict could not be dismissed. He said that this sparked the 4-3, 2-3 debate. Shah also defended the 2024 verdict in the reserved seats case , wherein PTI was declared eligible for seats reserved for women and minorities, in a setback to the ruling coalition. “We said that the PTI was a political party and it was wrong to deprive [them of their symbol] … and illegal,” he said, recalling that this was a decision “that nobody liked”. In a statement on Wednesday, the ECP referred to the remarks made by Shah, saying that they ignored “basic constitutional and legal facts related to the election matters and judicial decisions”. “It is highly inappropriate to present the judicial record for specific purposes through selective quotations, incomplete perspectives and one-sided interpretations,” the statement said. The electoral watchdog said that Shah had claimed that the SC’s majority decision about the elections in 2023 was a 4-3 verdict and that the suo motu notice and relevant petitions were dismissed. The ECP also stated that according to Shah’s claims, the election ruling was a “minority decision” and the commission could not have held polls. Regarding the PTI case, it said that Shah had declared the order for withdrawal of the party’s electoral symbol during the 2024 elections as “illegal”. The commission said that the election symbol was subject to transparent intra-party elections as per Sections 208 and 209 of the Election Act 2017. It added that “till date, PTI has not been able to fulfil the requirement”. The ECP said PTI was supposed to hold intra-party elections by June 30, 2021, and the commission had given the party three chances; however, the party failed to hold intra-party elections. As a result, the commission said that the party’s election symbol was withdrawn, which, the ECP added, was also upheld by the SC in 2025, along with rejecting review petitions filed by the PTI. The ECP further stated that PTI held intra-party elections after five years and its proceedings remained pending before the commission as the “PTI itself has taken a stay order from a high court”. It further stated that as per the commission’s records, the PTI was still enlisted as a political party. The ECP added that only political parties which contested the elections had a right to the reserved seats. “These political parties are required to submit a preferred list of candidates before the elections, while PTI has not submitted any preferred list,” it stated. It further stated that it was mandatory for a political party to win at least one seat and that independent members were not entitled to reserved seats and therefore, the ECP gave the seats to the eligible parties. It said that if the PTI was entitled to the reserved seats, then “Articles 51 and 106 of the Constitution and Section 104 of the Elections Act 2917 become ineffective”. The ECP said that it was “unfortunate” that a retired judge was taking a position against the Constitution and the law. In November 2025, Shah had resigned as an SC judge alongside Minallah, hours after the 27th Constitutional Amendment — which made significant changes to the country’s judicial system and established the Federal Constitutional Court — was signed into law by President Asif Ali Zardari. “By fracturing the unity of the nation’s apex court, it has crippled judicial independence and integrity, pushing the country back by decades,” he wrote in the letter sent to the president. “Staying on would not only amount to silent acquiescence in a constitutional wrong, but would also mean continuing to sit in a court whose constitutional voice has been muted,” he said.

items.title: Drone attacks kill civilians and cripple Sudan’s power infrastructure, UN warns of growing humanitarian toll
items.description: Drone attacks across Sudan have killed at least 14 civilians and injured several others, while strikes on electricity infrastructure have triggered widespread power cuts and disrupted clean water supplies, prompting warnings from the United Nations and the Arab League. The latest attacks killed eight people in Um Dibo, in El Sunut locality, West Kordofan, on Monday evening. Residents told Radio Dabanga that a drone strike also wounded three people. On Tuesday, at least four people were killed and more than 10 injured when a drone struck a fuel station in the middle of the market in El Abbasiya Tagali, South Kordofan. Witnesses told Radio Dabanga that the injured were taken to the town’s hospital. The strike also damaged the station and several vehicles. Other sources reported that the same drone hit facilities in nearby Rashad, although the targets and extent of the damage remained unclear. In Ed Damazin, the capital of Blue Nile region, drone attacks on several neighbourhoods killed a woman and a young man and wounded others on Tuesday evening, according to local sources. The strikes hit El Zahour, the Sudanese Armed Forces barracks area and El Ziraa El Aliya neighbourhoods, damaging a home. The Blue Nile Civil Society Initiative identified the woman as Ilham Ali Shikan, a mother of three, and said another woman, Amal Bashir, was wounded. The initiative blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and its ally, the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North, for the attack and called for an end to strikes on civilians and civilian infrastructure . Blue Nile governor Ahmed El Omda also condemned the attacks, describing them as an assault on civilians and civilian property. ‘UN warns of growing humanitarian toll’ The latest incidents come amid a wider campaign of drone strikes against electricity and fuel infrastructure across Sudan. The Arab League condemned repeated attacks it attributed to the RSF on energy facilities in Khartoum, El Gezira, Sennar, El Gedaref, River Nile and Red Sea states. The organisation said the strikes had severely damaged power facilities, knocked several out of service and cut electricity to large areas, worsening conditions for civilians . It warned that deliberately targeting power stations and other civilian infrastructure that does not constitute a military objective violates international humanitarian law and could amount to a war crime. The United Nations also warned that continued drone attacks on critical energy infrastructure were disrupting essential services. UN Secretary-General spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said on Monday that the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) was deeply concerned about the attacks and their impact on people across several states. According to reports cited by the UN, drones targeted two power stations in Kassala state and a substation in Merowe on Tuesday. Earlier attacks hit electricity facilities in River Nile state on Monday, a substation in Red Sea state on Saturday, and sites in North Kordofan and El Gezira. UN humanitarian partners warned that power cuts and fuel shortages had disrupted clean water supplies, forcing residents to rely on untreated sources and increasing the risk of waterborne diseases . Dujarric said the secretary-general strongly condemned the escalating drone attacks by parties to the conflict. In a statement issued two days earlier, the secretary-general said drone strikes had killed hundreds of civilians, including women and children, across Sudan and the Abyei a r ea , in what he described as a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law. He also condemned attacks on civilians and the critical infrastructure they depend on, including healthcare facilities, and urged the warring parties to agree to an immediate cessation of hostilities and engage in mediation efforts led by his personal envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto. The Arab League reiterated its support for Sudan’s unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity. Its secretary-general also appointed Zaid Al-Sabban as his personal envoy for Sudan. items.title: Kurt Okraku questions taxes on importation of national team equipments, gate proceeds
items.description: Ghana Football Association (GFA) President Kurt Okraku has asked the governement to consider granting tax exemptions on items imported for the service of the country’s national teams. Speaking before the Parliamentary Select Committee on Youth, Sports and Culture, Okraku said the taxes on equipments imported for national teams have become a burden to the administration. “Sometimes, the GFA is handicapped (and unable to pay for the cost of clearing its equipment). We dont have the finances.” The GFA President also criticised the Value Added Tax (VAT) rate of 17.5% that is charged on football tickets, questioning why other sectors of the economy like the entertainment industry, are not always required to pay similar rates for patronage of events. “We are charged 17.5 VAT at the gate on every game that we play. And yet, other entertainment providers are charged less. This is a problem that I’ve brought to the fore of leadership, not on one occasion, not twice, maybe more,” he said. Currently, government requires majority of state agencies, including private entities conducting business on behalf of the state, to comply with its tax laws. In the case of the Ghana Football Association, importation of items supplied by its technical partners such as PUMA all attract tax rates. These include match day jerseys, training jerseys, boots, training equipments, branding materials etc.

items.title: Au moins 15 pays européens ont été touchés par les cyberattaques visant les réfrigérateurs de supermarchés
items.description: Selon une analyse de la revue, au moins 15 pays européens ont été touchés par des cyberattaques visant les systèmes de réfrigération de supermarchés et d’entreprises alimentaires depuis le 11 octobre. Celles-ci ont d’abord concerné des supermarchés français, provoquant au moins plusieurs dizaines de millions d’euros de pertes, puis se sont étendues à d’autres pays début novembre. Des centaines de supermarchés français ont été touchés dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre, puis d’autres, équipés de contrôleurs Dixell permettant de piloter à distance la température des meubles frigorifiques et des chambres froides, dans la nuit du 12 au 13. Une seconde vague d’attaques a eu lieu dans la nuit du 1er au 2 novembre, touchant 14 pays, dont l’Allemagne, où des magasins Rewe et Edeka ont été visés, et l’Italie, où une vingtaine de magasins ont été touchés en Sicile, ainsi qu’une entreprise de restauration en Toscane. L’ampleur de ces attaques varie considérablement d’un pays à l’autre. La France se distingue des autres pays européens touchés : environ 700 supermarchés ont été visés, selon le gouvernement. Mis à part en Belgique, en Suède, en Italie, aux Pays-Bas et en Irlande, le nombre de magasins et d’entreprises visés dans les autres pays ne dépasse pas une dizaine. En Grèce et en Norvège, trois commerces ont affirmé avoir été touchés, bien que leurs cas n’aient pas été confirmés par les autorités. La piste d’une opération russe ou menée par des acteurs gravitant autour des services de renseignement de Moscou n’est pas à exclure. Selon l’entreprise américaine de cybersécurité Forescout, la plupart des quelque vingt attaques revendiquées depuis le début de l’année contre des systèmes de réfrigération l’ont été par des groupes d’hacktivistes prorusses Supermarkets Across Europe Report New Suspected Freezer Hack », Bloomberg , 2 novembre 2026.'> 1 . Xavier Bellekens, PDG de la firme de cybersécurité écossaise Lupovis, se dit quant à lui « fermement convaincu que cette activité pourrait être attribuée à un acteur malveillant soutenu par l’État russe » Supermarket Chain Thaw Massacre : Russia suspected in Europe’s fridge attacks », Politico , 3 novembre 2026.'> 2 . Selon Lupovis, des leurres (aussi appelés « honeypots ») mis en place par l’entreprise ont été ciblés par des attaquants dont les serveurs avaient déjà été utilisés par le passé par des groupes russes. Cette série d'attaques est d'autant plus troublante qu'aucune rançon n'a été demandée et qu'elle pourrait servir à envoyer un message aux gouvernements européens. Lundi 2 novembre, ce sont des chambres froides de l’Établissement français du sang (EFS) qui ont été touchées par une attaque visant leur prestataire frigorifique, leurs seuils de température ayant été « portés à de très hautes températures ». L’EFS assure que cette attaque n’a eu aucun impact sanitaire Une cyberattaque touche des installations frigorifiques utilisées par l'Etablissement français du sang, « sans impact » sur les échantillons conservés », FranceInfo , 4 novembre 2026.'> 3 . Les progrès de l’intelligence artificielle facilitent considérablement les opérations de cybercriminalité, et fournissent aux auteurs de nouvelles capacités pour mener des attaques à grande échelle en un temps réduit. CrowdStrike, dans un rapport publié en février, estime que le nombre d’attaques menées par des acteurs malveillants utilisant l’IA a presque doublé entre 2024 et 2025, augmentant de 89 %. Koudougou: 1 615 engins contrôlés, 834 non immatriculés dont 710 motos, 90 tricycles et 34 véhicules
items.description: A Koudougou, une équipe de la Direction générale des Transports terrestres et maritimes (DGTTM) a mené des contrôles, le mardi 3 novembre 2026. À l'issue de l’opération, il ressort que 1 615 véhicules ont été contrôlés, dont 1 361 motos, 166 tricycles et 88 véhicules à quatre roues. Parmi les véhicules contrôlés, 834 sont non immatriculés, dont 710 motos, 90 tricycles et 34 véhicules à quatre roues. A la suite des contrôles, 38 véhicules ont été mis en fourrière et 212 usagers verbalisés pour diverses infractions. Ce mardi 3 novembre 2026, une équipe de contrôle de la Direction générale des Transports terrestres et maritimes (DGTTM) a mené une opération de contrôle des immatriculations dans la ville de Koudougou. En collaboration avec la Police nationale, la Police municipale, la Direction régionale de la Mobilité et ses partenaires techniques, la DGTTM veut, à travers cette opération, s'assurer du respect des règles d'immatriculation, aussi bien chez les concessionnaires que chez les usagers de la route. Une démarche qui vise l'application des textes en vigueur, notamment la loi n° 53-94/ADP du 14 décembre 1994 fixant les règles relatives à l'immatriculation des véhicules automobiles, des remorques et semi-remorques ainsi que des cycles à moteur, et le décret n° 2017-0114 du 17 mars 2017 qui précise les conditions d'utilisation des séries d'immatriculation provisoires W et WW et des séries d'immatriculation définitives. À Koudougou, l'équipe conduite par la Directrice des Transports maritime, fluvial et de la Facilitation du Transit, la Camarade Adélaïde Anicha BANKA/KADIOGO, représentant le directeur général des Transports terrestres et maritimes, a fait une première escale chez Ibrahim SIEMDE. Visiblement inquiet à l'arrivée de l'équipe, le propriétaire des lieux s'est vite ravisé. « Quand ils sont arrivés, ils m'ont demandé l'agrément. Je l'ai présenté, j'étais très content. Ils m'ont encouragé. Personnellement, j'invite les commerçants qui n'ont pas d'agrément à tout faire pour l'obtenir, parce que cela rassure les clients et aide les Forces de défense et de sécurité dans leurs contrôles », a confié le concessionnaire, satisfait d'être en règle vis-à-vis de la loi. D'autres concessionnaires visités ont fièrement brandi leur agrément d'immatriculation provisoire. Néanmoins, quelques-uns sont encore à la traîne et l'équipe de contrôle les a invités à se rapprocher des services techniques de la Direction régionale de la Mobilité afin de bénéficier de l'accompagnement nécessaire pour l'obtention de leur agrément. Une fois l'étape des agréments passée, l'équipe a entamé la seconde phase de la mission, à savoir le contrôle des immatriculations (provisoires et définitives) dans les artères de la Cité du Cavalier Rouge. Au carrefour du lycée Joseph MOUKASSA, le superviseur des lieux, l'Adjudant de police Abdoul Kader KONSEIBO, plante le décor. « Au début, certains voulaient se plaindre, mais comme les spécialistes sont là, avec quelques explications, ils se rendent compte qu'en réalité, ils sont en infraction. Grâce à la sensibilisation des techniciens des transports, beaucoup nous ont promis de se mettre rapidement en règle. Ils disent en tout cas être en infraction par méconnaissance », a indiqué l'adjudant de police. Pour la cheffe de mission, la Camarade Anicha BANKA/KADIOGO, « c'est l'une des raisons de notre mission, qui est de sensibiliser les usagers à se mettre en règle, notamment à avoir leur immatriculation, qu'elle soit provisoire ou définitive. Je pense qu'avec ce contrôle, les uns et les autres vont prendre conscience, que ce soit au niveau des usagers, mais également au niveau des vendeurs de cycles, de la nécessité d'avoir l'immatriculation provisoire en attendant de faire l'immatriculation définitive », a-t-elle renchéri. À l'issue de cette opération de Koudougou, il ressort que 1 615 véhicules ont été contrôlés, dont 1 361 motos, 166 tricycles et 88 véhicules à quatre roues. Parmi les véhicules contrôlés, 834 sont non immatriculés, dont 710 motos, 90 tricycles et 34 véhicules à quatre roues. Enfin, 38 véhicules ont été mis en fourrière et 212 usagers verbalisés pour diverses infractions. Cette activité de contrôle, à l'image de celles menées à Ouagadougou et à Bobo-Dioulasso, permettra de sensibiliser les usagers de la route sur la nécessité de se mettre en règle en procédant à l'immatriculation de leurs engins, surtout en ces temps de forts défis sécuritaires que connaît notre pays. SCRP/DGTTM NB: Le titre et le chapeau sont de la rédaction. L’article Koudougou: 1 615 engins contrôlés, 834 non immatriculés dont 710 motos, 90 tricycles et 34 véhicules est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Texas Republicans Get Washed
items.description: America didn’t just get Blexas. America got Deep Blexas. The Democrat James Talarico beat his Republican opponent, Ken Paxton, by 12 points last night, a lead almost as large as Donald Trump’s margin over Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election. But Talarico wasn’t the only Democrat riding the wave: Governor Greg Abbott, who seemed to have an uncanny lock on the politics of the state, lost to Gina Hinojosa, who will become the first Hispanic governor of Texas. State Representative Vikki Goodwin ousted the powerful lieutenant governor, Dan Patrick. Nathan Johnson, a commercial litigator and state senator, will hold one of the most influential attorney general’s offices in the country after defeating his Republican opponent, Mayes Middleton. The Republican Bo French, who drew national attention for complaining about the presence of South Asian students at the University of Texas at Austin, lost his race for the Texas Railroad Commission to the Democrat Jon Rosenthal, who mocked French for a poll he posted on X last year : “The dude that posted the online poll last summer asking who’s a bigger threat to America, and the only two choices were Muslims and Jews—tonight this Jewish engineer sends that motherfucker home,” Rosenthal said on Election Night . Democrats appear to have narrowed Republican supermajorities on the Texas Supreme Court and State Board of Education, both bodies with national influence. Many Texas cases have ended up at the U.S. Supreme Court, and the educational standards set by the board can affect schools in other states because of Texas’s size and market power . Texas Republicans haven’t been washed like this since the end of Reconstruction, when Black Texans were overwhelmingly Republican and the state Democratic Party was run by a secessionist. The last time a Democrat won a Senate election in Texas, the Soviet Union was still in Afghanistan, Big Daddy Kane and Salt-N-Pepa had just released new albums, and Americans poured into theaters to watch that classic of American cinema, Crocodile Dundee II . [ Idrees Kahloon: Why Republicans lost so big ] The old saying is that the states are the laboratories of democracy. But for the past decade, Texas has been more of a laboratory for autocracy, testing out new forms of right-wing state repression. Texas has been an innovator in using voting restrictions and gerrymandering to entrench the power of the governing party. Texas lawmakers have pioneered restrictions on speech by passing book bans, censoring higher education, and demanding the firing of public servants whose views offend their sensibilities (such as the CEO of the Alamo Trust, who was forced out after a social-media post recognizing Indigenous Peoples’ Day). The state has pioneered draconian anti-abortion measures—passing its own strict ban with nearly unusable exceptions and a bounty law encouraging Texans to snitch on their neighbors, and also trying to bully other states into enforcing its anti-abortion laws. Texas lawmakers have engaged in the outright persecution of trans people and their families, including triggering investigations by the state’s Child Protective Services into parents if their child was suspected of transitioning. These Democratic wins mean that, at least temporarily, Texas will no longer be a safe environment for these kinds of experiments. The GOP plan to hold Texas hinged largely on heavy-handed gender politics ; a flood of ads attacked Talarico and Hinojosa for being too supportive of trans rights or, in Talarico’s case, of actually being transgender. Both candidates have moved to the right on trans-rights issues, but the ads clearly failed to mobilize voters. “We’re still running transgender ads. It’s just not resonating,” Dade Phelan, a Republican and former speaker of the Texas House, told Texas Monthly in October . “The 8 to 10 percent of voters in the middle who are going to decide this election, when they hear stuff about boys in girls’ sports, they don’t even know what you’re talking about. This never happened in their communities.” Texas is a very big place, and contrary to stereotype, liberal Texans have never been confined to Austin. For many years now, Republicans have consolidated their power by capitalizing on conservative fears that liberal infidels would “California my Texas.” In the end, it was Republicans’ success that led to their defeat. Republicans have run Texas for more than 30 years: There was simply no one else to blame for the economic burdens that drove Texans to the polls yesterday. Having so long dominated state politics, Republicans were used to trying to outflank one another from the right in GOP primaries, but ill-prepared for a competitive general election. They didn’t just lose the big races; they got walloped like Santa Anna at San Jacinto. As the more moderate, business-oriented party of the George W. Bush era gave way to Ken Paxtons and Bo Frenches, Texas Republicans seemed to become more focused on making the lives of millions of Texans miserable, rather than better. It was a strategy premised on the idea that disdain for out-groups and culture-war nonsense about vegan tacos and solar energy would be sufficient to distract Texans from corruption and misgovernance. It worked, until it didn’t. In his victory speech last night, Talarico addressed this strategy directly. “We are tired of being told to hate each other,” Talarico said. He might not have spoken for every Texan, but he was speaking for most of them.

items.title: Le Roi préside une séance de travail consacrée à la fin de mandat de la Minurso
items.description: Le Roi Mohammed VI, a présidé, ce mercredi 4 novembre, une séance de travail consacrée à la fin de mandat de la Minurso, indique un communiqué du Cabinet Royal. Voici le texte du communiqué : « Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L’assiste, a présidé, ce jour 04 novembre 2026 au Palais Royal de Rabat, une séance de travail consacrée au suivi de l’étape à venir après la fin des tâches de la mission des Nations Unies, à la suite de la non-reconduction de son mandat par le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU, lors de sa réunion tenue le 30 octobre 2026. Cette séance s’inscrit dans le cadre de l’Attention particulière que Sa Majesté le Roi, que Dieu Le préserve, n’a eu de cesse d’accorder à la cause de notre intégrité territoriale et de notre souveraineté nationale, illustrant ainsi Sa démarche sage, Sa vision clairvoyante et Son souci constant à sauvegarder les intérêts de Ses sujets au Sahara marocain. Au cours des travaux de cette séance, à laquelle ont pris part la Cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, le Conseiller de Sa Majesté le Roi, M. Fouad Ali El Himma, le ministre de l’Intérieur, Abdelouafi Laftit, et le Général de Corps d'Armée, Mohammed Berrid, Inspecteur Général des Forces Armées Royales (FAR) et Commandant la Zone Sud, Sa Majesté le Roi a mis l’accent sur les priorités contenues dans le communiqué du Cabinet Royal du 30 octobre dernier, à savoir le strict respect de l’intégrité territoriale du Royaume, de sa sécurité nationale et de la quiétude de ses citoyens, en particulier la population des provinces du Sud. Dans ce cadre, Sa Majesté le Roi, que Dieu L’assiste, a donné Ses Hautes Instructions pour la mise en œuvre ferme et vigilante de ces priorités, chacun selon son champ de compétences, à même de consolider le consensus national et de garantir la poursuite du projet de développement des provinces du Sud et des projets structurants y afférents, tout en veillant au suivi de tous les développements que connaîtra le dossier de notre cause nationale, à tous les niveaux, et conformément à la position officielle exprimée antérieurement. Tout cela en rappelant l’attachement ferme du Royaume au cessez-le-feu, un engagement volontariste qui ne changera pas avec la fin du mandat de la mission des Nations Unies qui a été incapable, à plusieurs reprises, de surveiller son respect et d’établir les effets qui découlent de sa violation. De même que le contexte de la création de cette mission et les fonctions initiales qui lui ont été confiées ont été dépassés, comme l’attestent les faits et les positions des acteurs internationaux. En concrétisation de la volonté du Royaume du Maroc d’accompagner l’étape suivant la fin des tâches de la mission onusienne, avec un esprit de responsabilité et de coopération avec l’Organisation des Nations Unies, Sa Majesté le Roi, que Dieu L’assiste, a donné Ses Hautes Instructions pour que le « Bureau de coordination avec la Minurso », relevant du ministère de l’Intérieur, se charge des missions de coordination et d’accompagnement de l’opération de liquidation et de retrait de ladite mission, à même de contribuer à la facilitation des différentes mesures inhérentes à cette opération et de garantir son déroulement dans des conditions fluides et ordonnées. Sa Majesté le Roi, que Dieu Le préserve, a aussi insisté, lors de cette séance, sur le respect par le Royaume de ses engagements internationaux et de sa doctrine diplomatique ayant pour socle le maintien de la paix et la contribution à son instauration et à sa réalisation par tous les moyens, tout en préservant la souveraineté du Royaume, et en gardant à l’esprit tous les changements positifs que notre cause nationale a connus et l’élan diplomatique l’ayant accompagné, couronné par la reconnaissance de la souveraineté du Maroc sur son Sahara par les pays amis et frères, qui considèrent l’autonomie comme la seule solution politique qui offre tous les composants pour clore définitivement ce conflit régional artificiel ». The post Le Roi préside une séance de travail consacrée à la fin de mandat de la Minurso appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Affaire des 3 tonnes d’or à la BCRG : « Cela me blesse que les gens pensent que j’ai détourné trois tonnes d’or », déclare Lounceny Nabé
items.description: L’ancien gouverneur de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG), Dr Lounceny Nabé, a comparu ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026 devant la chambre de jugement de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF). « C’est Affinor qui détient les trois tonnes d’or. Je n’ai aucun lien personnel avec eux. Cela me blesse que les gens pensent que j’ai détourné trois tonnes d’or. D’ailleurs, il y a eu une bataille de procédure dans cette affaire entre la Guinée et Affinor, et la Guinée l’a remportée. Par conséquent, je pense qu’on ne peut plus parler de détournement » Poursuivi dans une affaire portant sur la disparition présumée de trois tonnes d’or, évaluées à environ 200 millions de dollars, l’ancien patron de la BCRG a rejeté les accusations portées contre lui. Il soutient que l’or concerné se trouve toujours chez le raffineur belge Affinor. « Il y a eu une bataille de procédure dans cette affaire entre la Guinée et Affinor, et la Guinée l’a remportée. Par conséquent, je pense qu’on ne peut plus parler de détournement », a déclaré Dr Lounceny Nabé. L’ancien gouverneur est poursuivi à la suite d’une plainte de la BCRG pour des faits présumés de détournement de deniers publics, d’enrichissement illicite et de corruption. Il lui est reproché le détournement présumé de trois tonnes et 135 kilogrammes d’or destinées à la société Affinor, basée en Belgique, dans le cadre d’un contrat signé en 2015 portant sur l’affinage et la gestion d’une partie des réserves d’or de la République de Guinée. Interrogé sur les faits, le prévenu, qui a dirigé la BCRG de 2010 au 5 septembre 2021, a plaidé non coupable. « Je ne reconnais pas les faits. Je suis ici parce que j’ai été gouverneur de la BCRG à un moment donné. Je suis quelqu’un qui a toujours respecté la loi », a-t-il affirmé. Revenant sur les trois tonnes d’or au cœur de la procédure, Dr Lounceny Nabé a soutenu qu’elles n’avaient fait l’objet d'aucun détournement. Selon lui, elles ont été légalement transférées auprès du partenaire de la BCRG, le raffineur Affinor, dans le cadre d’une opération de monétisation, consistant à transformer l’or brut en or monétaire convertible en devises. « C’est Affinor qui détient les trois tonnes d’or. Je n’ai aucun lien personnel avec eux. Cela me blesse que les gens pensent que j’ai détourné trois tonnes d’or. D’ailleurs, il y a eu une bataille de procédure dans cette affaire entre la Guinée et Affinor, et la Guinée l’a remportée. Par conséquent, je pense qu’on ne peut plus parler de détournement », a-t-il insisté. Abordant la question de sa rémunération lorsqu’il était à la tête de la Banque centrale, l’ancien gouverneur a indiqué qu’il percevait un salaire mensuel d’environ 30 millions de francs guinéens, auquel s’ajoutaient certaines primes, notamment celles versées à l’occasion des fêtes. Il a également été interrogé sur son patrimoine. À ce sujet, Dr Lounceny Nabé a fait état de plusieurs biens immobiliers et comptes bancaires. « J’ai un compte bancaire à la BCRG depuis 1993, à l’époque où j’étais directeur général. J’ai un compte épargne à la Bicigui ouvert depuis les années 1990. J’ai une maison à Entag acquise en 1994, une maison à Matam depuis 2001, une maison familiale au village. J’ai un terrain à Sonfonia depuis 2001, un terrain à Kironty depuis 1998, un terrain à Manéah et un terrain à Kagbélen », a-t-il détaillé. L'ancien gouverneur devra répondre des faits qui lui sont reprochés devant la juridiction spécialisée. Elisa Camara L’article Affaire des 3 tonnes d’or à la BCRG : « Cela me blesse que les gens pensent que j’ai détourné trois tonnes d’or », déclare Lounceny Nabé est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Ghana’s 20 national teams rely on one broken bus – Kurt Okraku
items.description: Ghana Football Association President Kurt Okraku has shed light on some of the challenges facing the association in managing the country’s various national teams, calling for greater government support to ensure the long-term development of football. Okraku disclosed that all 20 national teams, including the Black Stars and Black Queens, rely on a single team bus purchased by the GFA 18 years ago. The bus, which was acquired in 2008, is now out of service, forcing the association to rent one during the most recent international window. Speaking about the challenges before Parliament’s Select Committee on Sports, Okraku described the situation as one of the fundamental problems preventing Ghana from building a sustainable and successful football ecosystem. “Your Black Stars, your Black Queens, and the 18 other national teams have access to one bus that was purchased by the GFA in 2008. Now the bus is broken. During the last international window, the GFA had to rent a bus. “If we want to create a sustained football ecosystem, these are the fundamentals. These are the reasons we have not had sustained and continuous victorious stories over generations. These are the hard truths,” he said.

items.title: Rugby à 7 féminin : l’Afrique sur le toit du monde aux JOJ Dakar 2026
items.description: Le continent africain a marqué de son empreinte le tournoi de rugby à 7 féminin des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026. Le Kenya, médaillé d’or, et Madagascar, troisième, ont porté haut les couleurs de l’Afrique, devant l’Australie, deuxième. Le rugby à 7 féminin a offert une belle consécration au sport africain à l’occasion des JOJ Dakar 2026. Au terme de la compétition, le Kenya a décroché la médaille d’or, tandis que Madagascar s’est hissé sur la troisième marche du podium. Entre les deux sélections africaines, l’Australie a dû se contenter de la médaille d’argent. La sélection kényane a confirmé sa supériorité en remportant la finale face aux Australiennes (17-12), au terme d’une rencontre disputée. Ce succès permet au Kenya de s’adjuger le titre et d’inscrire son nom au palmarès de cette édition des Jeux. Le parcours des Malgaches mérite également une attention particulière. En dominant la République tchèque (26-10) dans le match pour la troisième place, les joueuses de la Grande Île ont décroché le bronze. Une performance historique pour Madagascar, qui remporte ainsi sa toute première médaille olympique, toutes disciplines confondues. Cette double présence africaine sur le podium constitue un signal fort pour le développement du rugby féminin sur le continent. Elle récompense les efforts de formation et la progression de deux nations qui ont su rivaliser avec des équipes reconnues sur la scène internationale. Pour le Sénégal, pays hôte, le tournoi s'est achevé à la huitième place. Une première expérience à ce niveau pour les Lioncelles, qui auront pu mesurer le chemin à parcourir face à des adversaires de haut niveau. À Dakar, le Kenya et Madagascar ont ainsi offert à l'Afrique une double consécration. Au-delà des médailles, leurs performances donnent une nouvelle visibilité au rugby féminin africain et nourrissent des ambitions pour les prochaines échéances internationales.

VAST Ghana pushes for front-of-pack food warnings against unhealthy foods to tackle rising non-communicable diseases
items.description: The Executive Director of Vision for Accelerated Sustainable Development Ghana (VAST Ghana), Labram Musah, has called on the government to introduce stronger food policies, including mandatory front-of-pack warning labels, to help curb the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country. He said Ghana’s current food regulatory framework had gaps that allowed manufacturers to sell products high in sugar, salt and unhealthy fats without clear and standardised warnings to help consumers make informed choices. Speaking at a workshop on Nutrient Profile Modelling (NPM), Front-of-Pack Warning Labelling (FOPWL) and Healthy Food Policies in Ghana, organised by VAST Ghana in collaboration with SEND Ghana and GAND, Mr Musah said the increasing consumption of ultra-processed foods and sugar-sweetened beverages was contributing to serious health problems. He said that Ghana needed to move beyond dealing with unsafe or unhealthy products after they entered the market and focus more on preventive measures that would stop harmful products from reaching consumers in the first place. Mr Musah acknowledged the work of the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) in regulating food products but said more comprehensive policies were needed to strengthen the country’s food environment. “I wouldn’t say that the FDA is not doing their work. Let me say that they’re doing what they can do. That’s why sometimes you see that products in the market and the FDA will go there and get these products,” he said. However, he believes the country must adopt stronger standards to prevent manufacturers from producing and marketing foods with excessive amounts of ingredients that pose risks to public health. He said some products entering the Ghanaian market might receive regulatory approval without necessarily meeting the best international standards for protecting consumers. A major concern raised by Mr Musah was the absence of mandatory front-of-pack warning labels on food products in Ghana. He explained that the current system was largely voluntary, leaving manufacturers with considerable discretion over the nutritional information displayed on their products. According to him, this makes it difficult for consumers to know whether the food they are buying contains excessive amounts of sugar, salt or saturated fats. He called for an evidence-based Nutrient Profile Modelling system that would establish clear thresholds for determining when a product should carry a warning label. Under the proposed system, products exceeding the approved levels of certain ingredients would have clear warnings displayed on the front of their packaging. “We want to go beyond that, where we have a very robust system, a front-of-pack label backed by an evidence-based nutrient profiling system, where thresholds are properly developed by the FDA working with other relevant stakeholders,” he said. Mr Musah explained that the policy would allow consumers to identify products with high levels of unhealthy ingredients and decide whether they wanted to buy or consume them. He said clear labelling was particularly important because consumers needed to understand the nutritional content of the food they ate rather than depend on information they might not easily interpret. Mr Musah warned that the growing consumption of unhealthy foods was adding to Ghana’s non-communicable disease burden, which includes diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular diseases. He cited figures indicating that NCDs account for about 45 per cent of deaths in Ghana annually, describing the situation as a major public health concern. He said the government needed to place greater emphasis on prevention rather than relying mainly on healthcare interventions after people had developed chronic conditions. He referenced the Ghana Medical Trust Fund, introduced to support people living with chronic illnesses, including diabetes and hypertension, but argued that more attention must be given to preventing such conditions. He said the country could not sustainably address the growing burden of NCDs without policies that helped people make healthier food choices. “These are like firefighting approaches. So, can we go beyond that? And going beyond that means we need to come out with preventive measures. And one of the preventive measures is to ensure that people know what they’re consuming,” he said. He maintained that when consumers had clear information about the nutritional content of food products, they would be better placed to decide what to eat. Mr Musah called for other measures to discourage the consumption of unhealthy foods, including taxes on products high in sugar, salt and unhealthy fats. He said increasing the prices of such products could encourage consumers to reconsider their purchasing decisions. “When prices go up, consumers think twice before they buy the product,” he explained. He also called for stronger food procurement policies to ensure that government institutions, particularly schools, prioritised healthier food when purchasing meals for children. Under such a policy, he said, public institutions would be encouraged to procure nutritious food instead of products that could expose children to long-term health risks. Mr Musah further called for restrictions on the marketing of unhealthy foods, particularly advertisements targeting children and other vulnerable groups. He said the media and advertising industry had an important role to play in promoting healthier food choices rather than exposing children to excessive marketing of sugary drinks, snacks and other ultra-processed products. He said the proposed measures should work together to create a healthier food environment and reduce the risks associated with poor diets. Responding to whether the government was doing enough to support the campaign, Mr Musah said some progress had been made towards introducing stronger food policies. He disclosed that a Nutrient Profile Modelling system had been developed and was awaiting recommendations from the Ministry of Health. Once approved, the system would provide the necessary thresholds to help the FDA identify products that contained excessive amounts of sugar, salt and other ingredients of public health concern. He also revealed that four major food policy measures had been drafted and were undergoing review by the Ministry of Health. These include the Front-of-Pack Warning Labelling policy, restrictions on the marketing of unhealthy foods, fiscal measures such as taxes on unhealthy products, and public food procurement policies. Mr Musah expressed hope that the review process would be completed to allow the country to introduce stronger and more effective regulations. The VAST Ghana Executive Director also cautioned against allowing the interests of food manufacturers to undermine policies intended to protect public health. He argued that regulations must be strong enough to achieve their intended purpose rather than simply satisfy the concerns of industry players. According to him, the food industry could attempt to influence or weaken regulations to protect its commercial interests, making it important for policymakers to remain focused on public health. “You can have policies, but if it is not biting enough, then it’s better you don’t even have it. That’s what we are going for: a very robust, evidence-based policy, something that when it’s implemented, it can stand the test of time,” he said. He added that the success of a public health policy should not be measured by how comfortable manufacturers were with it but by its ability to change unhealthy practices and protect consumers. “If industry is happy that a policy has been enacted on food or any other unhealthy product, that means that these policies are not effective because it means that they are happy that they’ll be able to manoeuvre,” he said. Mr Musah urged civil society organisations, health professionals and the public to support efforts to get policymakers to speed up the approval process while ensuring that the final regulations were strong enough to deliver results. He said Ghana did not need to start developing standards from scratch, as international organisations had already produced evidence-based models and guidelines that could be adapted to the country’s needs. “The beauty is that they have already come out with the model. They’ve already come out with the guidelines. The standards have already been set. You don’t need to reinvent the wheel because it’s expensive,” he said.

items.title: Rafael Nadal rejoint la direction du Real Madrid
items.description: Rafael Nadal s’apprête à ouvrir un nouveau chapitre de sa carrière, cette fois loin des courts de tennis. L’ancien numéro un mondial va intégrer le conseil d’administration du Real Madrid, son club de cœur, sous réserve de la ratification de sa nomination par l’assemblée générale des membres délégués. Le conseil d’administration du club madrilène s’est réuni mercredi 4 novembre et a décidé de soumettre cette nomination à l’approbation de ses membres délégués. Une arrivée symbolique pour le Real Madrid, qui accueille ainsi l’une des figures les plus emblématiques du sport espagnol. Âgé de 40 ans, Rafael Nadal a marqué l’histoire du tennis avec un palmarès exceptionnel de 22 titres du Grand Chelem en simple, dont 14 à Roland-Garros, un record dans le tournoi parisien. Retraité depuis 2024, l’Espagnol reste étroitement lié au Real Madrid, dont il est membre honoraire depuis plusieurs années et qu’il soutient régulièrement depuis les tribunes du Santiago-Bernabéu. Dans son communiqué, le club madrilène a salué « l’une des plus grandes légendes de l’histoire du sport », soulignant également ses qualités humaines et son influence au-delà de ses performances sportives. « Pour le Real Madrid et pour tout le madridismo, c’est une immense fierté qu’une personnalité d’une telle envergure, tant sur le plan sportif qu’humain, rejoigne notre conseil d’administration » , a indiqué le club. Le Real Madrid a notamment mis en avant la détermination, l’humilité, l’esprit de compétition et le respect des adversaires qui ont caractérisé la carrière du champion espagnol. Des valeurs que Nadal a, selon le club, toujours incarnées et qui correspondent à l’identité madrilène. The post Rafael Nadal rejoint la direction du Real Madrid appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Lutte contre la fraude: plus de 95 millions F CFA de marchandises saisies
items.description: La Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la Fraude (CNLF), dans un écrit, sur sa page Facebook ce mercredi 4 novembre 2026, déclare la saisie de plus de 95 millions F CFA de marchandises frauduleuses saisies. «Grâce à la vigilance exemplaire et au professionnalisme des agents de la Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la Fraude (CNLF), un réseau de contrebande d'envergure vient d'être démantelé. L'opération révèle l'ampleur des menaces étouffées dans l'ombre. De Ouagadougou à Diébougou, c’est tout un système de fraude allant du cyanure aux denrées alimentaires de contrebande qui a été mis hors d'état de nuire par les hommes de Dr Mohamadi COMPAORE. Des saisies qui démontrent que la rigueur de la loi reste le plus sûr rempart de notre souveraineté. ​Ce coup de filet spectaculaire, couronné par une saisie globale de plus de 95 000 000 FCFA, illustre la détermination sans faille d'hommes et de femmes engagés au quotidien. Entre les 14 000 litres de gasoil interceptés, les cargaisons d'huile, les boissons illicites et les 55 tonnes de riz bloquées à Diébougou, chaque prise est une victoire pour la justice économique et la sécurité publique. Derrière ces chiffres impressionnants se cache surtout un engagement humain inestimable : celui d'agents qui, au péril parfois de leur quiétude, veillent à ce que la concurrence déloyale et les produits dangereux ne sapent pas les fondations de notre société. ​Face à ces résultats éclatants salués par Dr Mohamadi COMPAORE, coordonnateur national de lutte contre la fraude, le message est on ne peut plus clair : la fraude ne passera pas. Cette performance de la CNLF rappelle avec force que la probité et la vigilance demeurent nos meilleures armes pour bâtir un avenir plus juste, où chaque citoyen est protégé. Plus qu'un simple bilan chiffré, c'est une véritable promesse d'intégrité et un vibrant hommage à ceux qui, dans l'anonymat du devoir accompli, se tiennent chaque jour en première ligne pour défendre l'intérêt général.» CNLF L’article Lutte contre la fraude: plus de 95 millions F CFA de marchandises saisies est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Kurt Okraku challenges government over lack of investment in Ghana football
items.description: Ghana Football Association (GFA) President Kurt Okraku has questioned the government’s commitment to the long-term development of football in the country, insisting that sustained success requires more than the efforts of the football governing body. Ghanaian football has experienced a noticeable decline in recent years, with the fortunes of the various national teams and the Ghana Premier League coming under increasing scrutiny. Much of the criticism has been directed at the GFA over its management and development of the game. However, appearing before Parliament’s Select Committee on Sports on Wednesday, Okraku challenged the government to take greater responsibility, arguing that the lack of essential infrastructure and investment continues to undermine the country’s football ambitions. He acknowledged the GFA’s responsibility to provide logistics, improve playing surfaces, secure stadium facilities and recruit competent technical staff, but stressed that these measures alone cannot guarantee sustained success. “If we are to be honest, there is a lot more that brings sustained success in football. This includes continuous investment in grassroots football, continuous investment in coach education, exposing coaches to the international market, good scouting, and good facilities (football pitches) for the kids and senior teams to play. All this we don’t have in our country,” he said.
